d: Halted groups not in contact watch front, left, right and rear sectors.
Abort the attack (fallback or withdraw) when this share of the committed force is lost. 0 = off, only the band decides.
Base accuracy before modifiers. Higher = tighter impacts. Default 0.5.
On by default (tune_obj_phase_on = 1; 0 turns phases off). This objective is attacked only after the checked objectives meet Active Condition. Recon may still watch it.
When the Active After objectives count as done.
Reorganisation pause after the phase or Active After conditions are met, before the attack may start.
Seconds the objective stays active after the commander last processed it.
1 = armed vehicles look for new firing positions, shoot-and-scoot and fire at hidden enemies. 0 = old behaviour.
How quickly the commander reacts to changes on the battlefield.

A squad switches to assault posture with bounding fireteams when its weighted strength (MG, AT and vehicles count more; an armored vehicle facing infantry without AT always wins) is at least this many times the known enemy strength and it is not heavily suppressed. Also lets idle squads and Defend/Release garrisons leave their hold (within leash).
Distance in metres to a freshly seen enemy at which groups in aggressive posture stop advancing. Adjusted by the aggression slider.
Distance in metres to a freshly seen enemy at which groups in balanced posture stop advancing. Adjusted by the aggression slider.
Distance in metres to a freshly seen enemy at which groups in defensive, evasive or delay posture stop advancing. Adjusted by the aggression slider.

What happens after an overrun, home-lost or no-commander stop once the reason is gone. Back on = the spawner turns on again after Hold Time. Stays off = it stops for good. Out of men and Late in the mission always stop for good.
Low waits for recon before attacking, high attacks without recon.

On: the AI Aggression slider also scales the contact SOP engage distance, the close-target priority distance, the combat-move commit gate, the bounding deadlock wait, the assault commit distance and the commander staging and recon floors. Off: those systems use their fixed values and the slider only affects the systems it reached before.

t: Aggressive: Forward Bounds Rise With Aggression
d: During a firefight each soldier rolls every few seconds whether to bound to the next cover. Old rule: the roll used the take-cover chance, which the AI Aggression slider divides, so higher aggression meant FEWER bounds. New rule: chance = base take-cover chance x personality (Cautious 0.6, Measured 1.0, Aggressive 1.3, Reckless 1.5) x (0.6 + 0.4 x slider, max 2.0), x1.35 in the open, max 0.95. Bounds still end in cover.

When a seen enemy soldier 40-200 m away pulls back at least 5 m in about 3 s and has not fired for 3 s, the two nearest riflemen of the squad (not MG/AR) bound 10-30 m after him to cover, never ending closer than 40 m and never more than 150 m from their leader. The rest of the squad keeps firing. At most 3 pursuits per enemy; squad cooldown 30 s divided by the AI Aggression slider. Never on Defend/Garrison, indoors, during CQB, support-by-fire, hold fire, pinned or panicking.

Off: frag and grenade launcher usage = min(setting x AI Aggression slider x 2.5, 1), so at the default slider every usage of 0.4 or more is the same maximum. On: usage = 1 - (1 - setting)^(slider x 2.5), so lower settings still mean fewer grenades. Applies to newly spawned soldiers.

t: Aggressive: Return Fire At Unseen Shooters
d: When a soldier is fired on by a shooter he cannot see (15-400 m, cooldown 12 s), he fires back at the suspected position with chance 0.3 x (AI Aggression slider), max 0.7, instead of the tuned default (0). Never when pinned, in a vehicle or on Hold Fire.

When a soldier throws a frag at an enemy 10-35 m away and it bursts within 6 m of that enemy, the nearest squad mate within 15 m (not MG/AR) sprints crouched along the throw line to 8-12 m short of the enemy, never closer than 8 m to the burst. One rusher per throw; squad cooldown 20 s divided by the AI Aggression slider. Never on Defend/Garrison, indoors, during CQB, support-by-fire, hold fire, pinned or panicking.

t: Aggressive: Scale Soldiers With AI Aggression
d: Makes the AI Aggression slider change how soldiers fight, relative to today. At slider 1 nothing changes. Higher: shorter waits in cover (wait x slider^-0.7, at 2.5 about 50% shorter), shorter waits in the open, they close in nearer (min distance x slider^-0.5, at 2.5: 19/32/51 m for aggressive/balanced/defensive postures), tolerate more suppression before stress level 1 (x slider^0.3, max 0.9), and squads count as superior at a lower force ratio (2.0 / slider^0.5, floor 1.2). The engaged forward-bound chance also scales with slider^0.7 (before this, a higher slider gave FEWER bounds). Lower than 1 does the opposite. Default On. Pinned, grenade, friendly-lane and panic rules never change.

Overall AI aggression. 1 = DCO default (2.5x the old normal, effective value = slider x 2.5). Lower = soldiers take cover sooner, squads fall back sooner and the commander attacks less; higher = soldiers push through fire, squads hold under losses and the commander attacks more. New soldiers also roll more cautious or aggressive personalities. Can differ per faction.

How much DCO logic this squad runs. Full = everything. Balanced = no lean, window fire, awareness or rearm (cheaper). Light = only specialists, contact drills and explosion reactions (cheapest, use for far or background squads). Shows Custom when DCO features were changed by hand.
DCO features this squad runs. Turn off what the squad does not need to save server performance; the squad then behaves like vanilla for that part.

Enemy AI can hear players talking on VoN: certain within 8 m, fading to nothing around 25 m. Walls, vehicles, engine noise and nearby gunfire muffle it, longer talking is easier to hear, radio talkers are quieter. The listener group gets the estimated position as a contact.

Simulation detail for this group. Global default = commander groups follow the global AI LOD Mode, other groups stay vanilla. Vanilla / Keep awake (never fully asleep) / Always full apply to this group, with or without a commander. Applies immediately.

Simulation detail for groups owned by an AI Commander. Groups without a commander always stay vanilla unless their own AI LOD is set. Vanilla = engine decides (distant AI may stop). Prevent Max LOD = commander groups keep moving and fighting far from players. Full Detail = commander groups always at full simulation, heaviest. Applies immediately.
Friendly AI groups on the players' map. 0 = off, 1 = only squads supporting the player's group or sharing its objective, 2 = all.
Base radius (m) for objectives in the relevant overlay mode (objectives within 2x this radius are shown).

Auto: normal AI. Off: the AI of every member is switched off, they stand still, do not see, hear or react, cost no AI time, and enemy AI cannot perceive them; the Game Master can still take control of a member. Off + hidden: the same, and the members are no longer sent to players, so they are not rendered and cannot be seen or hit by players. Set back to Auto to wake the squad. Applies immediately and to members that join later.

Friendly AI squads near players report on the radio (text): breaking contact, pinned down, squad breaking in panic, lost contact and searching, and the commander's new main effort. Each message at most once per 90-120 s per squad.

Top speed for every AI-driven ground vehicle of this faction. 0 = engine default (AI drives as fast as the road allows). Lower values keep convoys together and reduce crashes. A squad's own Vehicle Speed Limit overrides this value.
Aim accuracy multiplier. Higher = more accurate.
How steady AI holds the weapon when standing, kneeling or tired. 1.0 = realistic; higher = smaller posture and fatigue penalty.
Seconds needed to reach full accuracy on a target.
Let soldiers keep aiming at the shooter while running to cover. Can differ per faction.
A squad counts as threatened when an enemy aircraft is within this many metres. Used only when air_threat_on is on.
Shots aimed upward steeper than this many degrees skip the friendly-fire lane check. Used only when air_threat_on is on.

On/off (1 = on). When on, AI treats enemy aircraft as threats and targets: squads go into contact when aircraft are near, may fire at them at longer range, and the long-range fire-rate limits for ground targets do not apply to aircraft.
Seconds a soldier stays at least vigilant after hearing gunfire within alert_gunfire_radius_m.
Distance in metres within which heard gunfire keeps a soldier at least vigilant for alert_after_gunfire_s.
Every faction in the faction manager may contest this objective.
Commit every squad to the offensive: no reserve and no defense share in BALANCED mode. Objectives under attack are still reinforced.
With All-in on, defenders of safe rear objectives (far from the front line) are also released to join the attack.
This squad may request artillery from the commander.
This squad may ask the commander for reinforcements when in contact.
This squad may be sent to help player requests (suppress, support, flank).
The commander may take a group off a less important task for a more valuable objective.
The commander may send this squad as reinforcement or threat response.

How this commander may hold its objectives when a threat comes within 600 m: Area defense (even odds), Defense in depth (outnumbered, falls back line by line), Reverse slope (hides behind a crest against armor or mortars), Perimeter (attack from several sides or isolated), Delay (badly outnumbered, trades ground for time). Spoiling attack hits enemies massing near the objective, Counterattack sends the reserve into the flank of a stalled attacker, Engagement area holds fire until the enemy reaches a trigger line on a road or open approach.

Tactics this commander may choose for an attack, picked by situation (intel, strength ratio, terrain, night, mortar) and personality. Pursuit runs after a capture, Delay is the defensive fighting withdrawal. If nothing allowed fits, Fire and Maneuver is used when allowed, otherwise the commander waits.

Jobs the AI commander may give this squad. Unchecked jobs are never assigned. Self-defence, panic and retreat always still happen. An empty list means the squad gets no commander jobs. Needs Commander Can Task.
Distance (m) inside which a soldier always turns to look at a shot. Can differ per faction.
Ambushed squads assault through (near) or take cover, smoke and break contact or flank (far).
What this squad does when ambushed while moving. Dynamic = close ambush: assault through; far ambush: cover off the fire line + smoke, then flank if stronger or break contact.
Most ambushes at the same time. The commander Max Ambushes is the hard limit.
Arc length (m) one sector covers. Smaller = more sectors.
Between the point limit and this: area fire (impacts spread over the uncertainty circle, +50% shells). Above it no HE: recon by day, illumination at night.
Armor is reported as armor only when identified within this distance (m). Can differ per faction.
Time from the order until catalog groups arrive. Groups do not exist until they arrive. If the area is blocked when they arrive they wait; Spawn anyway works for them too.
Distance (m) to the destination that counts as arrived. Can differ per faction.
Chance an artillery request is refused when the group is not recon or flank. Can differ per faction.
Seconds between artillery requests from the same group. Can differ per faction.
Contact size needed before a squad contact report also requests artillery (scaled by leader personality). Call-for-fire situations ignore it.
Friendly players within this radius (m) of an artillery target are warned before the rounds are fired.

When the commander releases an assault, the assaulting groups switch straight to the execute posture (move in and close with the enemy) instead of keeping their staging posture until each group re-evaluates.
Soldiers advancing toward a visible enemy closer than 30 m run instead of sprint and keep aiming, firing bursts while they move. Moves to cover under heavy fire stay a sprint.
1 = in Squad Fire and Maneuver, the assaulting team stops before the last 15 m and waits up to 15 s until the base-of-fire team has fired, so the final rush is covered. 0 = assault without waiting.
Rockets only against vehicles, bunkers, MG nests and window targets; flank armor, check backblast, squad covers the AT.
After an attack is aborted for lack of troops, seconds before the objective can be attacked again.

How long one attack attempt on an objective may run without capturing it before the commander counts it as failed. A failed attempt remembers its approach direction, demands more force next time and, after three failures, puts the objective on a 5 to 15 minute cooldown (by Patience) and leaves a screening ambush on the way out.

Use the Attack Only and Defend Only commander lists of objectives: attack-only commanders capture and then hand the objective over to a commander allowed to defend it; defend-only commanders never attack an objective the enemy holds. Off = the lists are ignored.
On by default (server tune obj.role_on; 0 turns roles off). These commanders attack this objective, then hold it only until a commander allowed to defend it has squads there, then they leave.

Effective own : enemy ratio (terrain and posture already counted) a planned attack needs. Below 0.9x this value for the hold time the commander asks for the missing men + 30% (USSR + 10%). Hasty attacks use the Hasty attack ratio.
Minimum own-to-enemy strength ratio needed by the most aggressive commander.
Minimum own-to-enemy strength ratio needed by the most cautious commander.
Most squads sent against one objective (staging, op plan and direct assault). The commander Max Attack Groups is the hard limit.
An attack does not start with fewer squads than this. The number itself comes from the force ratio.

Fire rule for attacking groups of this commander. Hold fire = only at enemies within about 50 m until the group is in contact. Tight = at relevant targets inside the engage distance. Free = at any target in range.
With Tight, attacking groups open fire at relevant targets inside this distance (m). The commander personality scales it a little.
On/off, default 0. Turning it on multiplies the advance stop distance by attacker_stop_dist_mul for attacking groups, so they close in further before stopping.
Multiplier (0.1-1) on the advance stop distance for attacking groups when attacker_close_in is on.

When a soldier of an attacking or flanking squad decides to move but has no fresh contact, he looks for cover toward the enemy instead of behind him. Squads that retreat, break contact or defend keep the old backward cover search.

t: Attackers: Close In To Assault Range
d: Squads on an attack task (ATTACK/FLANK, or Search and Destroy without a commander) keep advancing to assault range instead of stopping at the normal stop distance (30/50/80 m by posture). The stop distance is multiplied by attacker_stop_dist_mul (0.4 = 12/20/32 m). Soldiers under heavy fire still stop. Off = attackers stop at the normal distance.
Armed vehicle crews without an AI commander attach themselves to the nearest moving friendly squad and follow it. Off by default: crews placed by the Game Master stay where they are until ordered.

Squads pick their formation and spacing from the situation: wide wedge in open ground, staggered column in woods and towns, line on contact, echelon toward an enemy on the flank, tighter at night. Spacing is capped so nobody counts as a straggler. Off: formation follows the squad task only. Waypoint formation settings always win.
When a known enemy is 30-120 degrees off the direction of travel, squads in wedge or line switch to an echelon toward that side.
Squads in contact switch to a line so every rifle can fire forward.
Formation squads use in open ground when Auto Formation picks. Default logic = wedge, or echelon toward an enemy on the flank. Contact (line) and retreat still win.
At night squads close up one spacing step (wide to normal, normal to tight).
Formation squads use in towns, trenches and indoors when Auto Formation picks. Default logic = staggered column (column for recon).
Formation squads use in woods when Auto Formation picks. Default logic = staggered column.
An own objective at least this far (m) from contested ones can become a hub.
Spacing in open ground. Default logic = wide (10 m).
Spacing in towns, trenches and indoors. Default logic = tight (3 m).
Spacing in woods. Default logic = normal (6 m).

Finding a friendly body makes the squad sweep toward the killer. Lost enemies are chased along their last direction (150-300 m by personality) and the commander sends an idle group to cut them off. Under enemy artillery squads spread out, avoid halting in the open and do not bunch in one building. Static soldiers use concealment, avoid the skyline, keep back from windows, rest their weapon and deploy bipods.
Strategic value (0-100). Higher = more important.
A group needing a ride joins a trip already picking up if both pick-up and destination are within this distance.
Seconds after a trip starts that other groups can still join.

Objectives this commander ignores. This edits each objective's Commanders tab.
Fallback blocking position this far (m) outside the objective toward the threat.
On boarding timeout, the share of active passengers (leader required) that is enough to leave. Can differ per faction.
Distance (m) from the vehicle to the passengers that is close enough to start boarding. Can differ per faction.
Seconds allowed for boarding. Can differ per faction.
Withdrawals use smoke and fireteam leapfrog instead of one group run.

t: Break Contact: Squad Not Free For New Tasks
d: While a squad is breaking contact (withdrawing from a fight), the commander does not count it as a free reserve, so threat responses and other pickers cannot hand it a new task until it has finished. Off: a squad that stops for a moment during its withdrawal can be sent straight back toward the enemy.

On/off (1 = on). When on, a squad breaking contact first moves to a turn point off to the side before going to its rally point, instead of going straight. The turn is skipped if the point is off the navmesh or closer to the enemy.
Distance in metres from the squad to the break-contact turn point (clamped 20-200). Used only when break_contact_dogleg is on.
Largest turn angle in degrees off the straight line to the rally point. The angle is random between the min and max values. Used only when break_contact_dogleg is on.
Smallest turn angle in degrees off the straight line to the rally point. The angle is random between the min and max values. Used only when break_contact_dogleg is on.
Width in degrees of the fan of look directions after breaking contact. Used only when break_contact_face_threat is on.
Seconds the soldiers keep looking toward the enemy after reaching the rally point. Used only when break_contact_face_threat is on.
On/off (1 = on). When on, a squad that reaches its rally point after breaking contact turns its soldiers to watch toward the enemy, spread across a fan.
Seconds a squad stays marked combat-ineffective after breaking contact because it was depleted or shaken. A squad without a commander holds at its rally point during this time.

Fraction (0.1-0.9) of its peak strength at or below which a squad counts as depleted and may break contact on its own, depending on its retreat setting. Commander personality shifts it by 0.1 up or down.

On/off (1 = on). When on, the squad casualty thresholds for an evasive reaction (70%) and a step back (50%) scale with the raw aggression slider. When off they scale with the effective aggression (slider x 2.5), which at the default slider puts them near 95% and 90%.
On/off (1 = on). When on, a squad with the default retreat setting also breaks contact on its own when more than half of its living soldiers (at least 2) are Shaken or worse.
Briefing world markers. 0 = follow the player's level, 1 = off for everyone, 2 = on for everyone.
When a soldier identifies an enemy, nearby squad mates look and receive it as detected, with a voice callout.
Farthest distance (m) at which soldiers start trying to enter the building. Can differ per faction.
Scale the bullet counts above by personality: cautious soldiers react sooner, aggressive ones later. Can differ per faction.
Impacts needed before a soldier in the open runs for cover even though he has a target. Can differ per faction.
Impacts needed before a soldier in the open without a target runs for cover. Can differ per faction.
Impacts needed before a soldier in cover moves even though he has a target. Can differ per faction.
Impacts needed before a soldier in cover without a target moves to new cover. Can differ per faction.

How the AI commander learns about its own squads. 0 = Off (knows their state at once). 1 = Standard: squads report by radio (Contact, SPOTREP, LACE, SITREP) over one commander net and the commander plans with the last report. 2 = Full: Standard plus radio range (`tune_c2_radio_m` 1500 m without a radio pack), relay through another squad, radio check after `tune_c2_check_s` (600 s) of silence and lost contact (no new tasks, half strength, the squad holds `tune_c2_lost_hold_s` (300 s) and then moves to the nearest own objective). Can differ per faction. Other tuning: `tune_c2_sitrep_s` (300), `tune_c2_queue_max` (20), `tune_c2_tx_min_s` / `tune_c2_tx_max_s` (10 / 30), `tune_c2_sat_per_min` (4).
The commander may move this squad with trucks or transport teams.
Seconds between capture progress checks.
Seconds groups must hold the area to capture.
An objective is only captured when no building inside its radius is marked as occupied (enemy seen inside and not cleared yet).

Commanders update their enemy estimate for an objective carefully: a small contact lowers a large estimate only gradually, old memory without eyes on target cannot raise it, and unconfirmed estimates fade with a 10 minute half-life but never below half of the mission briefing.

The squad posture ladder (go defensive or evasive after casualties) uses the AI Aggression slider as shown in GM (1.0 = default: defensive at 50% losses, evasive at 70%). Off = it uses the internal aggression value, which makes squads stay aggressive until about 90-95% losses.
Seconds between census reports. Developer tool: shown only in Workbench, always off in normal games.

Server load census: every interval writes FPS, share of the frame spent in DCO scripts, AI/group/player population, event and RPC rates, queues and memory to dco.log (CENSUS channel) and census.log in the session folder $profile:DCO/Logs/<date>/<block>/session_<time>/. Also logs context for frames over 50 ms. Needs DCO Logging = Full. Not saved, off again after restart. Developer tool: shown only in Workbench, always off in normal games.

On: unarmed civilians react like frightened people instead of soldiers: they freeze briefly, run to a building or away from the shooting, hide, and calm down again after a few minutes. They are taken out of soldier behaviour (squad drills, contact reports, medics), and soldiers do not shoot at civilians unless one fires first. Off: civilians use the normal AI behaviour.

How careful this faction's soldiers are with explosives and area fire near civilians. 0 = Ignore: no extra holds for civilians (unarmed civilians are still never picked as targets). 1 = Normal: grenades, launchers and suppression are held when civilians are close to the impact or the line of fire, and mortars are held within 150 m of civilians. 2 = Strict: the same with 1.5 times larger distances. Set per faction to give each side its own attitude.
Seconds a civilian stays careful (walking, staying near cover) after hiding, before going back to normal.
Seconds a civilian stays hidden after the last shot nearby (longer after explosions) before carefully coming out.
On: non-military factions (for example civilians) may pick up weapons and ammunition from the ground and from bodies. Off: civilians leave weapons alone.

Seconds after contact is lost during which an enemy whose last known position is inside a building still starts the building clear. 0 = only enemies seen in the last 10 s (old behaviour). Example: 45 = the squad clears the house the enemy ran into instead of idling until it is seen again.

Squads attacking, flanking or in an overmatch assault that see enemies inside a building within 100 m clear it room by room in pairs (random order through the building graph), with a rear guard outside. Also sweeps buildings after an objective is captured. The Do CQB waypoint uses the same clear.
1 = attacking soldiers may still throw frag grenades at enemies within 35 m while under heavy fire (up to 2x the normal threat limit, never in panic). 0 = vanilla threat limit.
Distance (m) from the squad leader before a soldier out of combat is ordered to regroup. Also limits how wide the formation spreads (70% of it).
Multiplier on the cohesion distance.
In combat, a member farther than this from the leader in the open moves back to a random spot within half this distance of the leader. Scaled by each group's cohesion multiplier.
Same as Combat Cohesion (Open), used when the member or the leader is inside a building.

On/off (default on). Soldiers adapt fire mode, aiming, grenades, movement, bounding and threat to the range band to the enemy (contact <10 m, close 10-50 m, medium 50-200 m, long 200-400 m, extreme >400 m) and the terrain (open, forest, urban, indoor).
Low focuses on objectives, high chases enemy contacts.
How far (m) beyond its waypoint or objective radius a vehicle may go to find a firing position with line of sight.

Combat moves that are given as a direction (forward, left, right, back from the enemy) are turned into the real direction relative to the enemy before the soldier moves. Off = the engine uses the raw request position, which can send soldiers sideways or toward the enemy when they meant to fall back.

On/off (1 = on). When on, the pinned-soldier move block and the back-and-forth move detection judge a combat move by its direction type (forward, backward, flank) instead of only its raw move position.

Infantry escort tanks from behind or the side and lead them through towns and forest; tanks wait for infantry before entering towns or forest, go hull-down and fire at positions infantry spot. Defending squads in contact man nearby static HMG/AT weapons and the commander counts statics as defense assets.

DCO AI Commander that controls this group. Mortar team: place a mortar (or a mortar placement composition), then put a group of up to 4 soldiers with its leader within 40 m of it. Once the group has a commander it mans the mortar automatically. Transport team: a group of up to 3 soldiers driving an unarmed vehicle with 4+ free cargo seats becomes a transport team automatically.

Lets the AI Aggression slider shape commander timing: push, pursuit and consolidation waits and posture holds scale with the slider tempo, and offensive commanders set fewer ambushes. Also active whenever the K2 aggression scale is on.

How commanders read the AI Aggression slider. On: the slider is an odds multiplier (2 = twice the odds to attack or exploit, 0.5 = half) with a gradual tempo (up to 2x faster) and safety floors (staging 30 s, recon 90 s, attack ratio 1.3:1); attacks never start before staged groups arrive. Off: the older linear scale, where most commanders already hit the maximum at slider 1.

Seconds allowed for the drive. Can differ per faction.

If a player group enters the objective before release, all groups are released early to support it.
Percent per second control drifts back to the last owner when the radius is empty.
How fast soldiers spot and identify enemies. Multiplies the perception factor of every threat state. Default 1 = original speed, lower = slower, higher = faster.
Minimum threat score before a normal reinforcement is sent. Default 30.
Arc width (degrees) of the frontline when only one objective is held.
Smallest envelope arc radius (m) for small objectives.
Number of nodes on the envelope arc.
Envelope arc radius as a multiple of the objective radius.
Experience of groups taken from the faction catalog (empty force pool). Recruit, Regular, Veteran, Elite set the DCO skill Rookie, Regular, Veteran, Expert: aim, aim speed and morale.

Soldiers hit the dirt near blasts, get shocked and briefly deafened up close, react to friendly danger-close blasts, displace out of artillery beaten zones, report indirect fire to the commander (counter-battery also against player and vanilla mortars), take cover from grenade shrapnel and estimate where GL/RPG shots came from.
Extraction only if the group is farther than this (m) from the hub.

On: the commander sends a squad back to the logistics hub for extraction only when it is combat ineffective. A healthy squad that is only withdrawing (break contact, delay, OP withdraw) keeps its own fallback point and stays near its objective. Off: any withdrawing squad is also marched to the hub.
Faction this commander fights for. Changing it releases the groups and vehicles it currently controls.
Faction used by the Weakest / Nearest target modes. Any = all commanders. Greyed out when one specific commander is the target.

Close fights feel quicker. Under 30 m the first-shot delay is 0.2 s when under heavy fire (vanilla 0.8 s) and 0.15 s when surprised; a target that reappears within 10 s is engaged without delay. Aim settles in 0.35 s under 25 m (was 0.8 s), suppression and morale knock the aim back half as much up close, and small moves (under 3 m, under 30 degrees) no longer reset the aim. Longer ranges are unchanged.
How much a nearby enemy tank or armored vehicle lowers morale. -1 = automatic by faction: regular armies (US, USSR) 0.5, others (FIA militia) 1.0. Set it on a faction layer to override one side.
Seconds the feint runs before the main effort is released.
Feint or supporting-effort squads (0 = never feint).
1 = when no real cover is found, moving soldiers pick the nearest spot (dip, rock, tree, fence) that blocks fire from the enemy and go prone or crouch there. 0 = off.
1 = squad members spread their fire over different enemies instead of all shooting the same one (a target that is shooting at you still comes first, MGs may stack). 0 = off.

Fire rule for mortar teams of this commander. Hold fire = only at enemies within about 50 m until the group is in contact. Tight = at relevant targets inside the engage distance. Free = at any target in range.
With Tight, mortar teams open fire at relevant targets inside this distance (m). The commander personality scales it a little.

Threat-based fire discipline. The squad keeps moving to its objective and does not fire unless forced: more than 5 near misses on a soldier in a few seconds, an enemy inside its objective, or an enemy blocking its route. Only the threatened soldiers and 1-2 buddies fire; the whole squad fires if more than half is threatened or at the objective. Picking Hold Fire / Fire at Will / Return Fire turns it off.

t: Fire Support Needs Line Of Sight
d: When the support-by-fire position of a siege or attack-by-fire has no line of sight to the objective, the commander searches up to 27 positions on a ring around the objective for one that does; if none is found the old position is kept.

Soldiers who see an enemy within Fire While Moving Range keep the weapon up and fire while they shift, walk or jog a short move (up to 30 m), instead of lowering the weapon until they stop. Not while sprinting, crawling, panicking or dashing to cover under heavy fire. Moving fire is much less accurate. Can differ per faction.
Longest distance (m) to a seen enemy at which soldiers fire while moving. Machine guns are capped at 40 m. Can differ per faction.
Let soldiers fire (suppress) while running to cover. Can differ per faction.
Same as above for APCs.
With an AT soldier known, a soft-skin vehicle stays this long (s, +-25%) at one firing position before it moves.
Same as above for tanks.
Seconds after start before the commander makes his first decision.
The commander picks this squad first when it builds an attack (strong preference among squads that are fit and close enough, not an absolute order). Needs Commander Can Task.
Chance a bound goes to a flank position instead of straight forward. Can differ per faction.
Distance of the counter-flank position from the threat. Default 120.

Fire rule for flanking groups of this commander. Hold fire = only at enemies within about 50 m until the group is in contact. Tight = at relevant targets inside the engage distance. Free = at any target in range.
With Tight, flanking groups open fire at relevant targets inside this distance (m). The commander personality scales it a little.
Maximum distance (m) searched for cover when fleeing a position without cover. Can differ per faction.
These commanders attack this objective first. A commander focuses on one objective at a time; checking it here moves its focus away from its current one.
The objective this commander attacks first. None = the commander chooses.
IDLE groups still take AI Commander orders. Off = the commander leaves IDLE groups alone.

Attack even when the force ratio says the enemy is too strong or the doctrine says wait. Recon still runs (max 2 minutes) and at least 2 squads are still needed. Off = the focus waits until the commander has enough strength.
Attack the focus objective even when the force ratio says the enemy is too strong or the doctrine says wait. Recon still runs (max 2 minutes).

Formation for this squad. Auto = chosen by task and situation (needs Auto Formation on for the full logic). Any other choice is always used, even with Auto Formation off; spacing is still capped so nobody counts as a straggler.
Distance between soldiers in the formation for this squad. Auto = by terrain, contact and night.
Multiplier for the forward direction weight that comes from personality. Can differ per faction.
1 = The friendly fire lane check uses the real muzzle height of the shooter stance, so a prone or crouched friend below the line of fire does not block the shot. 0 = off.
Radius (m) for checking friendly presence.
No fire mission if friendlies are within this distance of the target. Default 25.
Where frontline nodes sit between our objective and the nearest threat (0 = ours, 1 = threat).
Seconds a group stays on frontline recon before returning to the pool.
Patrol radius (m) for recon groups sent to the frontline.
Most frontline recon squads out at once. The commander Max Frontline Recon is the hard limit.
Soldiers needed for full control change speed.
Allow roof and balcony slots.
Draw slots of used buildings (red window, orange roof, blue door guard, grey interior). Developer tool: shown only in Workbench, always off in normal games.
Defend: how far past the waypoint radius the flank team may go (meters). Default 50.
With no building in range, pick fighting positions in the field: cover, view toward the threat, off the skyline, in buddy pairs. Off = vanilla Defend.
One building at a time (windows then interior) or all windows of all buildings first.
Share of each building's slots to fill. Lower spreads the group over more buildings. Applies on the next garrison start.
Defend: soldiers in the flank team (one fireteam). 0 = no flank team. Default 4.
Spread soldiers over different floors. 0 = ignore floors, 1 = strong spread.
Soldiers of a garrison group who do not fit in the building slots get fighting positions in the field next to the building (scored for line of sight and cover) instead of standing around outside.
Maximum buildings per group. 0 = automatic.
Hold: never leaves the building. Defend: a small flank team may leave up to the leash. Release: garrison until triggered, then fight freely.
When only one soldier is left in a secondary building, move him to the group's main building.
Max seconds before a dead soldier's slot is refilled by someone from a less important slot.
Release: casualties (percent of the garrison) that lift the leash. 0 = off. Default 50.
Release: enemy this close to a garrison soldier lifts the leash (meters). 0 = off. Default 30.
Release: most of the garrison pinned down this long (seconds) lifts the leash. 0 = off. Default 20.
Release: go back into the buildings once it is calm again.
Seconds a soldier at a window sees no enemy while the group is in contact before he moves to a better window, preferring another floor. 0 = off.
A soldier pinned at a window for 8 s moves to another window, preferring another floor.

A garrison group starts taking its building positions as soon as part of it reaches the objective (instead of waiting for the whole group or a long timer), so defenders are inside before the attack arrives.
1 = every window faces the threat (waypoint rotation), 0 = spread evenly over 360.

Fire rule for garrison groups of this commander. Hold fire = only at enemies within about 50 m until the group is in contact. Tight = at relevant targets inside the engage distance. Free = at any target in range.
With Tight, garrison groups open fire at relevant targets inside this distance (m). The commander personality scales it a little.
Squads that garrison buildings on a held objective.
Underbarrel grenade launcher accuracy. Higher = tighter impact spread. 1 = default. Applies to AI spawned afterwards.
How often underbarrel grenade launchers are fired. 0 = never, 0.5 = default, 1 = often.

Who may save the current GM settings back to the server config file from the GM settings screen. Allowed values: "gm" (any Game Master), "admin" (server or session administrators, default), "off" (nobody). The listen-server host can always save unless this is "off".
A spot with this score is taken at once without searching on. The real maximum is about 0.87. Can differ per faction.
How often frag grenades are thrown. 0 = never, 0.5 = default, 1 = often.

Before throwing a grenade, soldiers also check where nearby friendlies will be when it explodes (their movement over the next 3.5 s) and add the throw scatter (10 % of the throw distance) to the blast radius. Fewer friendly-fire grenade deaths; some throws are skipped.
Two own groups closer than this (m) count as clustered.
Maximum number of saved group preset files the server keeps. When the count is reached, new preset uploads are refused until one is deleted.
Who may upload saved group presets to the server. Allowed values: "gm" (any Game Master, default), "admin" (server administrators only), "off" (nobody). Other values are ignored.
Groups spawned each time the spawner fires.

How far off soldiers are when they locate a shooter they only heard. 1 = realistic: the direction is off by 5-15 degrees and the distance by 15-50 % (more for faint, distant shots), and the error shrinks each time the same spot fires again, down to 30 %. Moving after firing starts a new estimate. 0 = soldiers know the exact spot from sound alone. The position is exact anyway when the shooter is seen, closer than 50 m, or at night when the muzzle flash is in view (not with a suppressor).
Which AI commanders may plan this objective: attack, defend, patrol, recon, reinforce and operation secondaries.
Own : enemy ratio an unplanned (hasty) attack needs. Below it the attacker asks for reinforcements before pushing. Planned attacks use the attack ratio.

Multiplies how often soldiers aim at the head instead of the body. Base chance by Skill Preset: Noob 2 %, Rookie 5 %, Regular 10 %, Veteran 18 %, Expert 25 %, Special Ops 33 %, Terminator 40 % up to 100 m, falling to 30 % of that at 300 m. 1 = default, 0 = never aim at the head, 2 = twice as often. Can differ per faction.

t: Heal Under Unseen Fire: Cover First
d: On/off (default on). A wounded soldier (more than 8 s before passing out) and a medic going to him wait with healing while an unseen shooter fired within 25 m in the last 6 s or hit near him; the soldier takes cover first. Critical bleeding is still treated at once.

On/off (1 = on). When on, a wounded soldier with more than 8 s until passing out delays healing itself (and seeks cover) while an unseen shooter recently fired at it from close range, and medics do not go to such a casualty.
Distance in metres within which a shooter the soldier cannot see counts as close fire for heal_unseen_gate. Used only when heal_unseen_gate is on.
Seconds after the last close unseen fire during which healing stays delayed. Used only when heal_unseen_gate is on.
Groups hear engines, footsteps, doors and explosions and turn to look or investigate.
Nearby gunfire (last 3 s: 40%, last 10 s: 70%) and running engines close by (50%) shorten how far soldiers hear. Rain and strong wind still apply.

What a squad hears becomes an estimate with a radius and confidence (logged heard_est). With Share Unseen Shooter Estimates on it is passed to nearby squads, and machine gunners use it to pick a fire position before contact.
Squads keep listening for footsteps, engines and doors while in a firefight, so an enemy flanking around them can be heard. Only sources the squad does not already see count.

Every soldier listens from his own position instead of only the squad leader. Footstep loudness depends on speed (walk 12 m, run 30 m, sprint 40 m), stance (crouch half, prone 30%) and ground (towns louder, woods quieter). Reloading is heard at 8 m, doors at 20 m. The soldier who hears it looks first, then the squad.
An enemy AT soldier closer than this (m) makes an APC (BTR, M113) pull back into cover.
An enemy AT soldier closer than this (m) makes an armed soft-skin vehicle (UAZ, Humvee) pull back into cover. Farther away it keeps fighting and shoots-and-scoots.
An enemy AT soldier closer than this (m) makes a tank pull back into cover.
Longest time (s) a vehicle stays hidden before it comes back out to a new firing position.
Shortest time (s) a vehicle stays hidden before it comes back out to a new firing position.
Maximum spotter-to-contact distance (m) for a high danger report. Can differ per faction.
Contact size that, together with a short distance, makes a squad artillery request ask for smoke instead of HE.
Threat score at or above which the cover move may not go forward toward the threat. Can differ per faction.
Seconds a strength band or a ratio shortfall must last before it counts, so short suppression or a brief panic does not trigger a request. Checked every 30 s, so 60 s means 60-90 s.
Auto = the nearest objective within 600 m held by the target faction when the mission starts. None = no home objective. Greyed out while Stop When Home Lost is off.
Faction whose commander uses this logistics hub. Auto = the nearest commander.
Seconds a casualty is treated at the hub before recovering.
How far (m) from the leader IDLE members search for cover or a building position.
Seconds a group without waypoints waits before going IDLE: members take cover and hold. Player groups never go IDLE.
IDLE units only leave their cover when an enemy is this close (m).

Fire rule for groups with no task of this commander. Hold fire = only at enemies within about 50 m until the group is in contact. Tight = at relevant targets inside the engage distance. Free = at any target in range.
With Tight, groups with no task open fire at relevant targets inside this distance (m). The commander personality scales it a little.
0 = flat random spread, 1 = strongly clustered at the centre.
Minimum seconds since this soldier's last cover move before an impact can start another. Can differ per faction.
Impacts always trigger a reaction even while another combat move runs. Can differ per faction.
If the group has a position waypoint, cover moves lean toward it. Can differ per faction.
Multiply the direction weights by personality. Can differ per faction.
Weight for taking the nearest cover in any direction. Can differ per faction.
Weight for running back, away from the threat. Can differ per faction.
Weight for running to the left, relative to the threat. Can differ per faction.
Weight for running to the right, relative to the threat. Can differ per faction.
Roll the DCO Dodge Chance (with personality scaling) before running to cover from impacts. Can differ per faction.
Look for a building first before normal cover when reacting to impacts. Can differ per faction.
Pick the cover direction at random using the weights below. Can differ per faction.
Hearing range multiplier for soldiers inside a vehicle. 0.5 = they hear shots at half the distance. Can differ per faction.
Distance in metres after which a broken soldier's withdrawal always ends. It also ends after 240 s.
Minimum distance in metres a soldier whose morale breaks withdraws. The withdrawal ends once it has gone this far and has not seen the enemy for 30 s.
Multiplier on how many spots are scored per behaviour tick. Higher = faster result, more server load. Can differ per faction.
Multiplier on the most spots scored before giving up. Can differ per faction.

Draws the indoor navigation graph of the building nearest to the camera (within 40 m): navmesh samples coloured by room, room labels, door nodes, stack points, numbered clear points and threat points (red door, orange stairs or hallway end, yellow window). 0 = off, 1 = rooms and points, 2 = also every link, 3 = also rejected samples (cyan = navmesh snapped away, white = building edge, dark = no floor below, magenta = floor is not part of the building, blue = no ceiling within 20 m, yellow = ceiling under 1.6 m). The graph is also saved to profile/DCO/IndoorNav. Debug only.
Multiplies the building search radius of indoor position searches (combat move indoors 70 m, idle take cover 50 m).
Max distance (m) the squad fires at infantry. Max 2500.

Every estimate carries its source (heard, seen by a teammate, reported), hop count and age. Older and second-hand information gets a wider search radius and lower confidence; grenadiers only fire 40 mm when confidence is at least 0.4.

How sure the commander must be about the enemy at an objective before he plans a real attack. Below this the enemy strength counts as Unknown and the doctrine falls back to recon, waiting or movement to contact. A contact report is worth 0.2 to 1.0 depending on how close the reporting squad was, and several squads reporting the same enemy add up. Lower values make the commander commit earlier on thin intel.
Radius (m) of intel this objective gives to other objectives nearby.
Seconds before intel counts as stale.
Commander intent map overlay (Dev/GM): plans, decision reasons, group roles, the commander's picture of the enemy. Off = none; on = Game Master only. Always allowed in Workbench.
Value of a firing line that only sweeps the interior, compared with one out of a window or door (1). Can differ per faction.
Chance this squad investigates an unidentified contact, rolled once per contact. Starts at the DCO global value.
Groups ignore unidentified contacts further than this (m).

How far off the AI's idea of an unidentified contact is, as a fraction of the distance to it. 0.12 = a contact glimpsed at 300 m is searched up to 36 m from where it really was, in a direction fixed per contact. Every new sighting shrinks the error. The search radius grows with the error and with the time since the last sighting. 0 = the AI always knows the exact spot. Set per faction.
This squad ignores unidentified contacts further than this (m). Starts at the DCO global value.
Score bonus for the spot the soldier already holds, so he does not hop for a slightly better one. Can differ per faction.
Best spots kept for the final check (if #1 is taken, #2 is used). Can differ per faction.
Mission time after which Stop Late In Mission stops the spawner. Greyed out while Stop Late In Mission is off.
Group confusion when the leader dies, report delay when the radio operator dies, grenadier smoke and HE use.

How well this soldier leads when he is the squad leader: Poor, Average, Good or Inspiring. Affects the morale his squad draws from him, how fast he rallies a panicking soldier, fire and ammo discipline, the force ratio his squad demands before attacking, and how hard his death hits the squad.
Relative share of new soldiers that roll Average leadership. Can differ per faction.
Relative share of new soldiers that roll Good leadership. Can differ per faction.
Relative share of new soldiers that roll Inspiring leadership. Can differ per faction.
Relative share of new soldiers that roll Poor leadership. Can differ per faction.

Soldiers lean out from cover to peek at unseen noise or fire, peek-shoot when suppressed, check where a lost target was last seen and watch sectors. In CQB they slice the pie at doors and corners, lean around hallway and stair turns and peek before entry, also while walking.

Soldiers remember, per map, where comrades were killed or wounded (15 m cells, per enemy direction, separately vs players and vs AI) and which spots gave hits while staying alive. Cover choice avoids learned kill zones and prefers proven spots, at most 25 % effect, with 12 % random exploration so nothing is avoided forever. Saved to profile/DCO/IndLearn every 5 min; test worlds learn in memory only.

AI remembers spots where it actually SAW a player firing or was hit by a player (with a rough position error that grows with distance). After two reports a soldier calls out the contact; idle alert soldiers then watch that spot and, if it was used 3+ times in the last 2 min, put suppressive fire on it. Only what the AI itself detected is used, never hidden player positions.
IDLE groups may leave cover to attack enemies that are fighting allies. Enemies shooting at the group itself are fought from cover.
IDLE groups may leave cover to investigate unidentified contacts.
Lethal radius (m) of a shell, added to the spread for the friendly safety radius.
Garrison growth follows the manpower budget. Refills are never limited.
Secondary objectives of this operation, in the same order as the objective list. Used only when Operation Primary is on. Ticking this objective itself is ignored. Shows the first 24 objectives.
Radius (m) for local friendly-versus-enemy strength around a threat.
Hot MEDEVAC / extraction jobs get an idle armored squad as escort.
Combat ineffective or retreating squads are picked up by a transport team and brought back to the hub.
Transport teams evacuate unconscious soldiers (no medic nearby) to the logistics hub, where they recover and return to this commander as a new reserve squad.
Transport teams whose vehicle has a resupply station bring ammo to squads running low. Off while global Magic Ammo is on.
Target beyond the weapon effective range and not directly threatened: stay put (prone if the target stays visible, else crouch) and fire slow aimed single shots.
Extra seconds after the move ends before the first look toward the threat. Can differ per faction.
Seconds between the repeated looks after reaching cover. Can differ per faction.
How many times the look after reaching cover is repeated so the view settles on the threat. Can differ per faction.
After reaching cover the soldier turns again toward the guessed shot position. Can differ per faction.
Head turns prefer the closest shot source and lock on it for a while, so soldiers do not flick between shooters. Can differ per faction.
Base chance to turn and look at a shot at the maximum look distance. Can differ per faction.
Longest delay (s) between hearing a shot and turning to look. Can differ per faction.
Shortest delay (s) between hearing a shot and turning to look. Can differ per faction.
Seconds the look direction stays locked after a shot. Further shots from the same source refresh it. Can differ per faction.
How often (s) the locked look direction is re-applied while the lock lasts. Can differ per faction.
A new shot source can take over the locked look only if it is closer than this ratio times the current source distance. Can differ per faction.
Maximum look priority bonus for a shot at distance 0, falling to 0 at the max look distance. Can differ per faction.
Extra look chance from the soldier's threat score (threat 0-1 times this value). Can differ per faction.
Spare magazines below this count as low ammo (half the group low = resupply).

t: Low Ammo: Compare To Own Loadout
d: A soldier counts as low on ammo only when he has fewer spare magazines than the minimum AND fewer than he started with. Off: the minimum alone decides, so MG gunners and AT/GL soldiers that start with 1-2 spares report low ammo before firing a shot.
When a heard shot is below the cover threat gate, a standing soldier crouches instead of doing nothing.
Safe distance (m) of landing zones and routes from threats.
Never runs out of magazines.
With Magic Magazine off, each AI reload has this chance to put one replacement magazine into the soldier's inventory. 0 = real ammunition only, 100 = same as Magic Magazine.
Spawn when the target commander's manpower drops below this many soldiers. 0 = off.
Marksmen take elevated overwatch, prioritize leaders, MG and AT, and relocate after a few shots.
Corrections in a row before the accuracy bonus stops growing.
Most player groups counted per objective; the rest are bonus.
Largest dispersion radius (m).
Longest time (s) a threat position is extrapolated from its movement.
Maximum groups scouting the frontline at the same time. Default 2.
Longest artillery cooldown.
Most groups this commander sends against one objective. Server JSON maxAttackGroups overrides it at start.
Distance (m) beyond which soldiers no longer turn to look at shots. Can differ per faction.
How many medics one group lends out at the same time.
Farthest (m) an idle group may be pulled to patrol.
Most requests in the queue before the overload penalty.
Maximum groups sent to one threat cluster. Default 2.
Most seconds an attack release is held because of a threat on the flank.
Most sweep waypoints created per group inside an objective.
Largest number of defence sectors per captured objective. Sector count = perimeter / Arc per Sector x personality, kept between Min and Max.

Longest travel time (without the 60 s buffer) the commander accepts for a player group. Longer: it offers transport (accept on the radial); with no transport or no answer the group keeps its task as a bonus the operation does not wait for.
Default for every commander's maximum number of groups sent on one attack (1-20). -1 keeps each commander's own setting from its prefab or the GM.
Seconds to load each casualty. Can differ per faction.
How far (m) to look for a medic from another group for a bleeding casualty.
How far (m) to look for a medic from another group for an unconscious casualty.
Seconds before a lent medic counts as failed and another medic is tried.
Unconscious casualties may be reached under fire, with smoke, when the medic is not directly engaged. Bleeding casualties always wait until it is safe.
Friendly players are treated by AI medics too.

On/off (default on). Machine gunners (MG and AR) keep their suppressive fire rate and suppress-last-known window even when their own threat level is low; the base of fire follows its task, not the gunner's fear.
Machine guns may keep bursting (suppression) up to this range; beyond it they fire slowly.
Machine gunners set a base of fire, keep suppressing the last known position, displace and get an assistant.
1 = MG/AR gunners are not moved by Trigger-Based Movement during contact, so they keep their firing position instead of leaving it to advance. 0 = MG gunners move like riflemen.
1 = in contact, the fireteam with the MG/AR does not take bounding turns and keeps firing; it only moves up when the rest of the squad is more than 40 m ahead. 0 = MG teams bound like other teams.
Smallest dispersion radius (m).
Minimum distance (m) to spots other soldiers have booked. Can differ per faction.
Ordinary infantry needed before a report. AT, MG, snipers and vehicles are always reported. Can differ per faction.
Shortest artillery cooldown.
Minimum ceiling height (m). Rejects crawl spaces. Can differ per faction.
Below this intel confidence the commander does not ask for troops on an enemy estimate; it asks for a recon team instead. Up to 0.6 the request is routine and the estimate is padded.
Minimum seconds before re-reporting a contact only because the information is fresher. Can differ per faction.
Combined cluster score needed before any active response (reinforcement, flank, artillery). Default 25.
Minimum defence sectors per objective.
Base cooldown after a fire mission. Total cooldown is clamped to 30-300 s. Default 60.
Morale of catalog groups. Low: break sooner (x0.8) and start tense. High: hold longer (x1.2).
Groups with average morale above this (0 fresh, 3.7 broken) get no attack tasks.

Morale stress a soldier takes when a bullet actually hits him (a second hit within 30 s counts half, at most one hit every 3 s). Bleeding adds its own stress on top. 0 = being hit does not affect morale, only suppression and injuries do. Set per faction.

Maximum morale a soldier can gain from support around him: squad mates within 30 m, a living leader within 100 m, a calm leader within 30 m and another friendly squad within 100 m. Each of these subtracts from his stress. Panic needs stress above about 2.4, so a high cap makes panic and break almost impossible in a massed force. Set per faction.
Morale stress added when an enemy is endangering (aiming or firing at) the soldier, at most once every 5 s.
Extra morale stress added per second while a soldier's threat state is alerted.
Seconds after the last bad event before a soldier's morale can step back to a calmer state.
Half-life in seconds of morale stress from events (casualties, unseen shooters and similar) and of morale relief.
Multiplier on morale stress from bad events and incoming fire while the soldier is in cover. Below 1 means cover reduces morale loss.
Maximum seconds a soldier stays panicked. When reached, stress is cut below the panic level and the soldier drops to shaken. 0 = no limit.
Seconds after a forced panic release during which the soldier cannot panic again (stays at most shaken).
Morale stress level at which a soldier panics (other levels: tense 0.4, shaken 1.5, break 3.7), scaled by personality and skill. Higher means panic later.
Morale stress added per second while a soldier is pinned.
Seconds a soldier's threat state must stay at vigilant or lower before calm morale recovery starts.
Fraction of suppression stress removed per second for each nearby friendly soldier. Applies at all times.
Fraction of suppression stress removed per second once the soldier has been calm for morale_recover_calm_s and not hit by suppression for 4 s.
Morale stress added per second while a soldier is suppressed.
Extra morale stress added per second while a soldier's threat state is threatened.
Maximum mortar range (m).
Minimum mortar range (m).
Objective name (max 32 characters), used in debug overlays and logs. Empty falls back to the entity name.
Commander name (max 32 characters), shown in the group Commander dropdown. Must be unique; a name already taken is rejected.
Gaps narrower than this (m) count as narrow. Can differ per faction.
Most ticks to wait for a navmesh tile to load before giving up. Can differ per faction.
Base size of idle reserve patrols: patrol centres are placed 2-6x this distance from their anchor objective, and the route radius is about 1-2.6x this value.
Angle difference (degrees) between a new shooter and the current threat that counts as a new direction. Can differ per faction.

At night: squads in contact with unlit enemies 100-400 m away fire a flare (from a 40mm illumination round or RSP-30 in their inventory; otherwise they ask the commander for illumination), defending groups open fire later, long-range fire starts closer, and the commander fires illumination over an objective when the assault is released.
At night, a squad artillery request asks for illumination instead of HE when its report quality (lower with distance and darkness) is below this.
At night Defend/Garrison groups open fire at this fraction of their normal engage distance (unless directly threatened), and rifle/MG effective range is scaled by the same factor.
Minimum time between flares from the same squad. Only one flare per 150 m area at a time.
At night AI flashlights stay off outdoors and only the entry team clearing a building turns them on inside. Vehicle headlights go off when an enemy is known within 800 m.
Position error multiplier at night. Can differ per faction.
Spotting speed on the darkest night, as a fraction of daylight speed. Moonlit nights and dusk fall between this value and 1. Default 0.25.

At night soldiers spot and identify enemies more slowly, scaled by the real light level (moon, clouds, dusk). Enemies lit by flares or lights stay easy to see. Hearing gunfire is not affected, so a shooter still gives away his position. Off: soldiers see at night as well as by day.
1 = A soldier keeps his last move direction for a few seconds and does not reverse it right away, which stops back-and-forth stepping. 0 = off.
Friendly players in voice or radio range get a small notification when an AI squad shares a contact. Each player can hide it in Settings > DCO.
Spawn when the trigger objective is lost or captured by the target commander's faction.

Use the Phase / Active After settings of objectives: a side attacks phase N only after it holds every objective of the earlier phases (then waits Active Delay). Off = every objective can be attacked at any time. Only matters when a mission sets phases on its objectives.
Most objectives attacked at the same time. The commander Objectives At Once is the hard limit.
How many enemy / neutral objectives this commander works on at once (attack, staging, recon). -1 = follow the doctrine preset; 1-10 = override the doctrine with this value.
A building marked occupied counts as clear after this long without new contact from it, so captures never stall.
A spot is rejected when another soldier is this close (m). Can differ per faction.
Most observation and listening posts at once, including doctrine and perimeter OPs. The commander Max OP is the hard limit.

t: Open Ground: Get Off The Open
d: A soldier caught standing still in the open while vigilant or under fire rushes to the nearest cover or, with no cover near, goes prone and crawls. Also applies when shaken. Off = only alerted, calm soldiers use the open-ground rule.
Maximum cover search distance in metres for suppressed, shaken or pinned soldiers on bounding, open-area and suppressive-fire moves.
Seconds a calm soldier may stay stopped in the open (not in cover, not in a building) before the open-ground rule moves it to cover. Doubled when prone.

On/off (1 = on). When on, the open-ground rule starts from the Vigilant threat state instead of Alerted, also applies to pinned soldiers, and in open terrain sends the soldier directly to the nearest cover found instead of leaving prone soldiers in place.
Seconds a suppressed or shaken soldier may stay stopped in the open (not in cover, not in a building) before the open-ground rule moves it to cover. Doubled when prone.
Multiplier on how long a soldier waits before its next combat move while it is in an open area. When tune_agg_profile is on, a higher aggression slider lowers it (result clamped 0.8-5).
Percent losses that turn a supporting capture into a fix, commit the reserve, or shift the main effort.
Anchor of an operation: when a commander picks one of its secondaries, it plans the whole operation around this objective.
Players within this radius (m) of an objective hear the commander's operation broadcasts.
Percent change in an objective's defender estimate that can trigger a re-plan (must hold 60 s and change the ratio band).
Seconds without progress on the current main objective before the commander shifts its main effort.
Before the main assault is released, a supporting squad fakes an attack on a nearby objective and/or smoke is fired on the far side, to pull enemy reserves away.
A soldier with only 2 spare magazines who is not under heavy threat takes magazines from a body within 10 m that no recently seen enemy can see. Normal rearm still starts at 1 magazine.

A soldier who has been lying still in the open for the stalemate time while trading fire with a visible enemy 20-200 m away bounds to the nearest cover towards the enemy, or 10-25 m forward when there is none. Not while suppressed, pinned or when too many squad mates are already moving.

An enemy 40-150 m away who has not shot at this soldier for 5 s and faces more than 60 degrees away is a chance: if visible he gets +2 target score, if not the soldier moves 15-30 m to cover 30-60 degrees off the line, on the side behind the enemy shoulder. At most 1 in 4 of the squad moves at once; cooldown 20 s divided by the AI Aggression slider.

Riflemen prefer enemies caught in the open: open ground +3, moving faster than 1.5 m/s +2, standing +1 (max +5) on top of the normal target score. An enemy shooting at them still comes first. Aim settles 30% faster on an exposed or running target.

Every 2 s a soldier with a frag checks the squad picture for 2 or more enemies within 5 m of each other at 5-40 m and throws if the arc is clear and no friend is in the blast. Before this only the current target was checked.

Against a target over 50 m away whose body is hidden and only the head shows, a rifleman holds aim instead of spraying, and fires the moment the enemy moves, stands or shows fully, or after 6 s. Not for MG/AR or support-by-fire squads.

When a squad mate is firing at the same enemy and that enemy has not fired for 6 s (divided by the AI Aggression slider), the soldier bounds 10-25 m forward to cover, stopping 20 m short. At most half the squad moves at once (more with higher aggression); cooldown 15 s divided by aggression. Never on Defend/Garrison, indoors, during CQB or support-by-fire.
When a visible enemy 15-60 m away is reloading, the soldier sprints 6-15 m forward to cover. At most half the squad moves at once; cooldown 10 s divided by the AI Aggression slider.
Seconds a soldier may lie still in the open exchanging fire before Break Stalemates moves him. Divided by AI Aggression.

A squad that clearly outguns a confirmed enemy (weighted strength: MG, AT and vehicles count more; ratio scaled by leader personality) keeps bounding forward while the enemy is still visible instead of trading fire from position. Aborts on a new unknown contact, fire from another direction, heavy suppression or when the edge is lost.
Overmatch assault only starts when the enemy is closer than this.
Control percent needed to become owner.
Control percent at which ownership is lost.

On: a panicking soldier picks one of several reactions weighted by personality: run to cover, flatten and stay down, run to the nearest calm squad mate, or fire a wild burst toward the shooter and drop. He bolts again (up to 3 legs) when shot at during the panic and may pop smoke before running. Off: the old single reaction, run or crawl to cover. Under 15 m he always fights. Set per faction.
Morale stress every squad mate within 20 m takes the moment a soldier panics, on top of the slow contagion from standing near a panicking soldier. 0 = a panic does not spread. Set per faction.
If the nearest enemy is closer than this many metres when a soldier panics, it skips the panic freeze and keeps fighting instead of fleeing.
Maximum distance in metres a panicking soldier flees to find cover when the enemy is beyond panic_mid_m. Also the maximum length of one panic sprint.
Longest time in seconds a soldier freezes and does not fire when it starts to panic. The actual time is random between panic_freeze_min_s and panic_freeze_max_s.

Shortest time in seconds a soldier freezes and does not fire when it starts to panic. The actual time is random between panic_freeze_min_s and panic_freeze_max_s; no freeze if the enemy is closer than panic_close_m.

A panicking soldier whose nearest enemy is between panic_close_m and this many metres goes prone and rushes to cover within rush_cover_max_m. Beyond this distance it flees to cover up to panic_flight_max_m away.
Longest time in seconds a panicking soldier with an enemy at mid range (between panic_close_m and panic_mid_m) does not fire at targets more than 15 m away. Random between the min and max values.
Shortest time in seconds a panicking soldier with an enemy at mid range (between panic_close_m and panic_mid_m) does not fire at targets more than 15 m away. Random between the min and max values.
Longest time in seconds a panicking soldier fleeing from a far enemy does not fire at targets more than 15 m away. Random between panic_nofire_min_s and panic_nofire_max_s.
Shortest time in seconds a panicking soldier fleeing from a far enemy does not fire at targets more than 15 m away. Random between panic_nofire_min_s and panic_nofire_max_s.
Low reallocates groups quickly, high waits longer.
Metres the patrol centre moves toward the frontline each think. 0 = fixed.
Patrol centres stop drifting this close (m) to the nearest enemy objective.
A new patrol centre is too similar if closer than this (m) to a remembered one.
How many recent patrol centres each group remembers.
Patrol radius multiplier for a full group (12).
Patrol radius multiplier for the smallest group.
Points rated for terrain per think, shared by all idle groups.
Patrol points shift to higher ground with better view.
Most reserve squads that patrol at once; the rest stand by.

Fire rule for patrols of this commander. Hold fire = only at enemies within about 50 m until the group is in contact. Tight = at relevant targets inside the engage distance. Free = at any target in range.
With Tight, patrols open fire at relevant targets inside this distance (m). The commander personality scales it a little.
Spotting multiplier. Higher = detects enemies faster and further.
Multiplier on perception speed while a soldier is panicked or broken.
Multiplier on perception speed while a soldier's morale is shaken.
Perception speed factor used while a soldier is in the threatened state. Lower means slower spotting and identification.

Server-side profiler: every 30 s writes FPS (avg/min/longest frame), AI count by LOD, groups per commander, time per DCO system and queries/raycasts per second to dco.log (PERF channel) and perf.log in the session folder $profile:DCO/Logs/<date>/<block>/session_<time>/; frames over 50 ms list the systems that ran. Near-zero cost when off.
Combat style: Cautious, Measured, Aggressive or Reckless.

Personality of this commander, separate from the doctrine: Measured (1/1/1/1/1, Calculated, Moderate), Careful (1.5/1.5/0.5/1.5/1.5, Careful, Moderate), Bold (0.5/0.5/2/1/1, Bold, Fast), Scout (2/1.5/1/1/1.5, Calculated, Moderate). Picking one sets the traits below.
Relative share of new soldiers that roll the Aggressive personality. Can differ per faction.
Relative share of new soldiers that roll the Cautious personality. Can differ per faction.
Relative share of new soldiers that roll the Measured personality. Can differ per faction.
Relative share of new soldiers that roll the Reckless personality. Can differ per faction.

On by default (server setting tune_obj_phase_on = 1; 0 turns phases off). Phase N is attacked only after this side holds every objective of phases 1 to N-1 (then waits Active Delay). Always active = no gating. Owned objectives are always defended.

Accurate close fire (weighted near misses) pins soldiers down: they stay low, stop moving and only fire rare unaimed bursts until the fire stops, then peek and recover. When half the squad is pinned the leader reports, pops smoke, the free fireteam suppresses and flanks, and support is requested.
Maximum distance in metres a pinned soldier crawls (prone) in one move.
Total near-miss weight within 3 s that pins a soldier who is in cover. Same personality, posture and aggression changes as pinned_threshold_open.

Total near-miss weight within 3 s that pins a soldier who is not in cover. Changed by personality (cautious x0.7, aggressive x1.2, reckless x1.4), aggressive group posture (x1.5) and aggression. Only used when the pinned behaviour is enabled.
Empty primary with an enemy under 10 m: switch to the handgun instead of reloading, switch back when clear.
Minutes a player group stays bonus only after hitting the fail limit.

Highest briefing HUD level players may pick. 0 = Hardcore (radio subtitles only), 1 = Standard (orders tab), 2 = Assisted (orders card). Limits Show orders as, Markers in the world and Draw on the map in each player's settings.
Multiplier on player group travel time (distance / speed times this, plus margin).
Seconds added to the player group travel time.
Failed accepts or ETAs in a row before a player group becomes bonus only.
Highest briefing HUD level players may choose. 0 = Hardcore, 1 = Standard, 2 = Assisted.
Commander briefings to player groups (OPORD, FRAGO, phases, withdraw/cancel). Off = nothing is sent and players see Disabled by server.
Target position known within this many meters: point fire mission (tight sheaf). Used by threat response, prep fires, counter-battery and squad calls for fire.
Base position error (m) of a shared contact per 100 m between the spotter and the enemy.
Threat position uncertainty grows this many metres per second of intel age.
How accurate the first picture of the enemy is at the start: Accurate (confidence 0.8, +-10 %), Normal (0.55, +-30 %), Weak (0.35, +-60 %, still Unknown) or None.
Look for a building first before normal cover. Off = go straight to the nearest cover. Can differ per faction.
Seconds between censuses of the objective radius.

What makes this spawner spawn. One-shot: everything once at start. Counterattack wave: 2 groups when the home objective is lost. Steady top-up: a group whenever the commander drops below 60% strength. Commander on call: a group whenever the commander asks (recommended). Custom: set the triggers yourself; the trigger rows below are greyed out unless Custom is chosen.
Set by the server config (groupPresetUploads = gm / admin / off; groupPresetLimit, default 200 presets). Changing it here has no effect.
Load a commander preset from the server folder $profile:DCO/CommanderPresets. Keys missing from the file stay unchanged. The first entry shows the active preset; * means it was edited after loading.
Save all settings of this commander as a preset file on the server (letters, digits, _ and -, max 32). To overwrite an existing preset other than the active one, end the name with !
Below this share the request becomes priority (normal arrival time). USSR commanders do not ask above this value; below it they ask for one whole group. FIA uses this value + 0.1.
Threat score at which reinforcement is prioritized. Default 70.
Job priority for deploy (attack, flank, recon, suppress).
Largest penalty for objectives beyond the relevant distance.
Job priority for extraction.
Job priority for medevac.
Minimum priority of player requests (transport, extract, medevac).
Most points from being close to the commander.
Job priority for redeploy and long patrols.
Job priority for reinforcement.
Distance (m) from the commander at which the proximity bonus reaches 0.
Job priority for resupply.
Most enemies counted for the score.
Lowest threat scale, so far enemies never count as zero.
How fast the threat score falls with distance (1 = same as proximity).
Points per enemy before distance scaling.
Chance an AI is allowed to go prone, in every situation. 0 = AI never go prone, 1 = always allowed. Each AI keeps its roll for 10 seconds; AI already prone stay prone.

Realistic prone moves: crawl forward up to 15 m (under heavy fire, sneaking, MG/marksman shifts), roll sideways up to 3 m, crawl back up to 5 m still facing the enemy. Longer prone moves get up to crouch first.
Soldiers go prone only when they are threatened, under fire, suppressed, in an ambush or evasive posture, or are machine gunners with a target. Other prone requests become crouch.
Soldiers who fall far behind their leader are ordered back. Can differ per faction.
Minimum seconds before the same group can be pulled again.
The new objective must be this many times more valuable than the group's current task.
Let the assault push enter a building when the target is inside. Can differ per faction.
Milliseconds between re-evaluations of the assault push. Can differ per faction.
Extra cooldown per request while the queue is full.
Seconds to process each request before the next one.
Longest radio delay (s) before a report reaches the commander. Can differ per faction.
Shortest radio delay (s) before a report reaches the commander. Can differ per faction.
Position error multiplier for contacts passed by short radio.
Capture area radius. Units inside count toward control of the objective. Towns 100-150 m, a farm or crossroads 40-60 m. The ring is drawn in the world while the objective is selected.
Pick the cover direction at random using the weights below (back / left / right / anywhere). Can differ per faction.
At start, vary every trait by up to 0.5 and courage/decision by one step around the personality preset.
How soldiers react to bullets landing 2-3 m away (impacts under 2 m are handled separately).

Soldiers need a short moment before firing at a newly seen enemy (longer when relaxed, shorter when alert, faster with higher skill, slower when the enemy is behind them). A first near miss on a relaxed soldier makes him freeze or drop for a moment.
Use the realistic hearing model: hearing range, score-based head turns, delayed reaction and direction error. Off = the old instant reaction. Can differ per faction.
Soldiers low on ammo resupply from ammo boxes, logistics trucks and corpses.
Rearm may use enemy corpses.

t: Rearm: Stop At Own Loadout / Full Inventory
d: A rearming soldier stops when he is back at the spare magazines he spawned with, or when his inventory has no room for more (MG belts), instead of trying until timeout. Off: rearm only ends at 3 spare magazines, so MG gunners keep trying until timeout.
Ammo budget for recon by fire on APC autocannons.
Ammo budget for recon by fire on MG-armed vehicles.
1 = vehicle gunners fire short bursts at the last known enemy position when the enemy is hidden.
Seconds between standing recon reports of nearby enemies.
How long the commander waits for a mandatory recon report before it gives up. On Unknown it then uses Movement to Contact when allowed, otherwise Wait or skip.
Most seconds to wait for recon confirmation before attacking anyway.

Fire rule for recon groups of this commander. Hold fire = only at enemies within about 50 m until the group is in contact. Tight = at relevant targets inside the engage distance. Free = at any target in range.
Recon squads sent to an unknown objective (0 = no recon before attacking).
With Tight, recon groups open fire at relevant targets inside this distance (m). The commander personality scales it a little.
Without a friendly group in contact, reinforcements stop this far (m) from the threat.
Most squads sent to help one threatened area. The commander Max Reinforcement Sent is the hard limit.

Fire rule for reinforcing groups of this commander. Hold fire = only at enemies within about 50 m until the group is in contact. Tight = at relevant targets inside the engage distance. Free = at any target in range.
