With Tight, reinforcing groups open fire at relevant targets inside this distance (m). The commander personality scales it a little.
Seconds between reinforcements to the same cluster. Default 120.
Points left for Commander Spawners set to take points. Separate from the soldier stock. -1 = unlimited.
Recon and flank squads ask the commander for reinforcements when they see at least this many fresh enemies (scaled by leader personality).
Seconds before a reinforcement request is reset even if nobody came. Can differ per faction.
Soldiers left for Commander Spawners that use the stock. -1 = unlimited.
Reject spots in narrow gaps (open door frames, bent corridors). Can differ per faction.
Chance a fire mission request is randomly refused. 0 = never, 1 = always. Default 0.1.
1 = only direct. 2 = a squad that received a contact may pass it on once more (with extra error).
Tactical reload below 30% when no enemy was seen for 3 s, fireteam mates do not reload at the same time, 'reloading' callout.
Distance (m) of the extra threat sample points left and right of the threat. 0 = one point. Can differ per faction.
Defending: weight of the threat score against the general spot score. Can differ per faction.
Fire position: weight of the threat score against the general spot score. Can differ per faction.
Defending: candidate spots closer to the threat than the current one by more than this (m) are rejected. Can differ per faction.

Needs Learn Player Firing Spots. Confirmed player spots are saved per map as 15 m cells and, next session, only make alert soldiers glance at them (no aiming or firing). Memory fades by 30 % each session. Off: spots are forgotten when the mission ends.
A contact counts as new information if it moved more than this (m). Can differ per faction.
Position error (m) in reports per 100 m between spotter and contact. Can differ per faction.
Reports can only be sent if a group member carries a radio. Can differ per faction.
Maximum distance (m) searched for new cover when repositioning from cover. Can differ per faction.
Seconds before a queued request expires.
A spot needs at least one firing direction (outside or a long interior line). Off helps in packed buildings. Can differ per faction.
Short radio sharing only works when both the sender and the receiver carry a radio. Voice always works.

What this commander does with free reserve squads. 0 = they wait where they are. 1 = one QRF squad is kept near the staging area, or near the threatened objective when defending. 2 = QRF plus link patrols between own objectives, observation posts on both flanks, a counter-attack ambush and local defence of newly captured objectives. At most half of the free reserves are used; the rest stay available.
Share of the force the commander always keeps in reserve instead of committing it to attacks, recon or flanks. Also sets how many idle squads BALANCED mode keeps for defense. 0 = no reserve.
Share of the commander's manpower held back when Keep reserve applies (0.33 = one third). The GM reserve policy still applies; All-in overrides it.
Most squads kept back as reserve.
Squads always kept back (only when at least min + 2 squads are available). The share comes from Reserve Share.
Low retreats easily, high keeps fighting.
If the soldier is already moving to cover, do not start a new move unless the fire comes from a new direction. Can differ per faction.
Seconds the response record (reinforcement count, cooldowns) per area is kept.
Most seconds one response runs without result before it times out.
Seconds a found spot stays valid before it is searched again. Can differ per faction.
1 = A short relocation that gets interrupted is resumed instead of being dropped. 0 = off.
Seconds to hand supplies to a group. Can differ per faction.
Most magazines given to each soldier on resupply. Can differ per faction.
Hold this objective until overrun: the doctrine delay, fallback and withdraw rules are ignored for its defenders.
When this squad breaks contact on its own (smoke, fireteams leapfrog back, regroup at a rally point). Default = overrun or 40% strength left; Cautious commanders retreat earlier, Aggressive later.
After dropping passengers the vehicle drives back to its rally point (hub). Can differ per faction.
Chance (0-1) that a soldier shot at by a shooter it cannot see returns suppressive fire toward the estimated shooter position. 0 = never, unless tune_agg_retfire raises it.
Minimum seconds between unseen-shooter return-fire attempts by the same soldier.
Maximum distance in metres to the shooter for unseen-shooter return fire (minimum is 15 m).
Beyond this range rifle fire rate is capped (slow single shots); threat cannot raise it.
Low needs clear intel, high attacks even when blind.

On/off (default on). Before a squad that lost contact indoors hands the building to room clearing, the building is checked with the CQB planner; buildings that cannot be planned (no outside door, no rooms) are skipped and searched from outside instead. Needs Combat Context on.
One intermediate waypoint every this many metres of travel.
How far (m) an intermediate waypoint may shift sideways to find a safer spot.

Below this share of its peak combat strength (0-1) the commander counts as worn down and asks for replacements at routine priority (double arrival time, only when nothing else waits). At or above it, no request. Combat strength counts the wounded, unconscious, panicked and low on ammo for less, and MGs and vehicles for more. FIA uses this value + 0.1.
Longest time in seconds a calm soldier runs on one combat bound. The actual time is random between rush_calm_min_s and rush_calm_max_s.
Shortest time in seconds a calm soldier runs on one combat bound. The actual time is random between rush_calm_min_s and rush_calm_max_s and also caps the bound length (time x run speed).
Maximum distance in metres to a cover spot that a soldier caught in open terrain will rush to. Also the cover search radius for a panicking soldier whose enemy is at mid range (see panic_mid_m).
Cover closer than this many metres is reached by crawling instead of a crouched sprint. Pinned or panicking soldiers, and soldiers with no squadmate covering fire, always crawl.
If the nearest enemy is within this many metres, a soldier caught in the open does not rush to cover and goes prone and crawls instead.
Longest time in seconds a suppressed or shaken soldier runs on one combat bound. The actual time is random between rush_shaken_min_s and rush_shaken_max_s.
Shortest time in seconds a suppressed or shaken soldier runs on one combat bound. The actual time is random between rush_shaken_min_s and rush_shaken_max_s and also caps the bound length.
No spawn while players or enemies are within this distance. Spawns wait and retry. Drawn in the world while Game Master is open: light = clear, orange = waiting, red = off or stopped.
Height (m) of a sampling cell, about one floor. Can differ per faction.
Horizontal size (m) of the sampling grid. Smaller = more thorough, more candidates. Can differ per faction.

On/off (1 = on). Soldiers ordered to suppress (group suppression, support-by-fire task or return fire) keep firing at the area even without seeing the enemy, if the near part of the fire lane is clear.
For area fire at an unseen enemy (sbf_area_fire), the first this-many metres of the line from the soldier toward the target area must be free of obstacles, otherwise it does not fire.
Threat score added per detected enemy.
Objectives within this distance of this primary are planned as its secondaries (unless Linked Secondaries are set).
Sector multiplier for the most careful commander (more sectors).
Sector multiplier for the most eager commander (fewer sectors).
Scale the sector count by the commander's personality.
This squad reports enemy contacts to the commander.
Rested: full strength. Reduced: arrives tired (stamina 50%) and short on ammo (60% of spare magazines, at least 1).

Squads pass their estimate of an unseen shooter (from incoming fire) to friendly squads in voice or radio range, with delay and extra error per hop. Machine gunners and grenadiers of the other squad can then suppress a shooter they never saw. Uses the contact sharing ranges, radio rule and hop count.
Shared contacts are marked on friendly players' maps (vanilla AI enemy markers). Positions keep their error.
How often (seconds) the commander checks the artillery queue for a mission to fire.
Same as above for APCs.
Between the hide distance and this distance (m) from an AT soldier, a soft-skin vehicle keeps firing but moves to a new firing position after each exposure period.
Same as above for tanks.
Distance (m) of squad-to-squad short radio.
Extra direction error (degrees) added for shots that were barely audible. Can differ per faction.
Smallest error (degrees) when a soldier guesses where a shot came from. Can differ per faction.
Enemies needed to report the contact as a platoon. Can differ per faction.
Enemies needed to report the contact as a squad (fewer = several). Can differ per faction.
Combat skill preset, from Noob to Terminator.
1 = AI do not use a post or loiter spot (smart action) that lies within 1.5 m of barbed wire or an anti-personnel mine, so they do not get cut standing there. 0 = off.

Before a squad starts clearing a building, check its indoor navigation graph. Buildings that cannot be planned (no outside door, empty or no rooms) are skipped and the squad picks another building. Off = the squad tries, aborts and retries that building later (cqb_plan_fail_retry_s in the server config).
Do not send a new cover move while one from this reaction is still running. Can differ per faction.
How often smoke is thrown to cover movement. 0 = never, 0.5 = default, 1 = often. Applies to AI spawned afterwards.
Throw smoke when retreating from a position without cover (needs a smoke grenade). Can differ per faction.
Spawn once shortly after the mission starts.
Groups spawn at a free spot within this radius of the spawner. Drawn as a green ring in the world while Game Master is open.

A Commander Spawner placed during the mission with the Custom preset and no trigger switches to Commander on call and sends one group right away, so it works without any setup. Off: a new spawner stays idle until you pick a preset.
Show the Commander Spawner cards to Game Masters: placed, waiting, off, no trigger, groups ordered and arrived. Off hides every card; the spawner keeps working and still logs.
Game Master master switch. Off cancels the orders on the way and returns their stock; no condition turns it back on, only the Game Master.
Total AI cap per faction for Commander Spawners. When reached, spawning is delayed. 0 = unlimited.

Specialists run their own combat behavior during a fight. MG and AR: move to the chosen fire position, drop prone and unfold the bipod, settle, then fire bursts at seen enemies or traverse suppression over the estimated position; AR moves in short 3-5 s rushes and gives covering fire while a teammate bounds. AT: stays on the launcher job against armor and launcher targets, flanks and shifts for backblast. Marksman: holds the overwatch spot watching the sector and relocates after 2-3 shots. Grenadier: lobs 40 mm at unseen shooters 35-300 m away. It outranks the normal attack behavior but gives way when an enemy is closer than 25 m, when bleeding, pinned, panicking, on hold fire or under another order. Off: the gunner uses the older relocate + suppress steps. Can differ per faction.
A rifleman picks up the weapon of a fallen MG/AT/GL specialist when the group needs it.

1 = fireteams bound only when the other team is set and has fired (covering fire), and the covering team keeps suppressing the last known enemy spot while the other moves. 0 = old time-sliced bounding.
Friendly players in voice or radio range get a small notification when an AI squad shares a contact. Each player can hide it in Settings > DCO.
AI squads share enemy contacts with nearby friendly squads by voice or short radio, without going through the commander.

1 = an attacking squad in contact at 50-300 m splits: the team with the MG/AR becomes base of fire, the other team bounds around a flank and assaults at 40 m. Needs Squad Bounding Handshake = 1. 0 = off.

A squad in contact breaks contact (fire and movement back to a rally point) when most of its soldiers are shaken or worse, and stays combat ineffective for 150 s. Off = squads only break contact when overrun or depleted.
Allow several squads to use the same building for indoor positions (defend, idle, garrison). Off = one building per squad.
Extra distance (m) outside the objective radius for the staging point.
Maximum staging distance (m) from the objective.
Minimum staging distance (m) from the objective.
Staging point distance from the objective as a fraction of the commander-to-objective distance.
Stalemate: control changes less than this percent...
Seconds before the stalemate response can trigger again on the same objective.
...for this many seconds.
Force a standing stance while running to cover. Can differ per faction.
Soldiers available to a Commander Spawner that uses stock. -1 = unlimited.
On/off (true/false, default true). When on, the first unrestricted Game Master is offered the list of saved Global settings presets to load at session start, if any presets exist.

A soldier on a static weapon (HMG, AGL) also gets off when the weapon is destroyed, when it has been empty for 8 s, or when he is under threat from an enemy within 150 m that is 15 degrees or more outside the gun traverse arc. Off: he only gets off when an enemy is within 15 m.
Stops for good after Late Minutes of mission time.
Off while the home objective is not held by the commander's faction.
Off while more enemies than friends (at least 2) are inside the safe radius for the hold time. Counts living conscious soldiers; vehicle crews count as men; a crewed enemy armored vehicle adds 4.
Off while there is no commander to feed. With Weakest or Nearest it first switches to another commander of the faction.
Seconds without getting 3 m closer to the leader that count as stuck. He tries another point once, then is marked stuck.
Seconds outside cohesion distance before a soldier is pulled back. Can differ per faction.
Log each straggler: distance, active behavior, combat mode, cover, leash. For diagnosis.

How much this objective matters to the commanders. High counts its base value x1.67, Moderate unchanged, Low x0.5, No = not a goal on its own (it is still fought over when enemies near it threaten or block).
Fire mortars or artillery for a group that meets one of the checked conditions (artillery safety rules still apply).
Fire mortars or artillery for a group that meets one of the checked conditions (artillery safety rules still apply). Shown dimmed with the Faction tag while it follows the faction.
Send medevac when a group meets one of the checked conditions.
Send medevac when a group meets one of the checked conditions. Shown dimmed with the Faction tag while it follows the faction.
Send reinforcements when a group meets one of the checked conditions. Overran never sends reinforcements into a lost position.
Send reinforcements when a group meets one of the checked conditions. Overran never sends reinforcements into a lost position. Shown dimmed with the Faction tag while it follows the faction.
Send a resupply job when a group meets one of the checked conditions.
Send a resupply job when a group meets one of the checked conditions. Shown dimmed with the Faction tag while it follows the faction.
Send support (QRF, relief or armour support) when a group meets one of the checked conditions.
Send support (QRF, relief or armour support) when a group meets one of the checked conditions. Shown dimmed with the Faction tag while it follows the faction.

Fire rule for support-by-fire groups of this commander. Hold fire = only at enemies within about 50 m until the group is in contact. Tight = at relevant targets inside the engage distance. Free = at any target in range.
With Tight, support-by-fire groups open fire at relevant targets inside this distance (m). The commander personality scales it a little.

Needs Learn Player Firing Spots. On: a spot the player used 3+ times within 2 min gets a short burst of suppressive fire from an alert soldier with no visible target, at most once per 20 s per spot. Off: soldiers only watch the spot.

Soldiers keep firing at the last seen position of a hidden enemy for a window based on weapon (rifle 5 s, MG 12 s, close 8 s) and personality, spread along the cover edge, then watch the spot and report lost contact.
Position error multiplier while the group is suppressed. Can differ per faction.
Radio delay multiplier while the group is suppressed. Can differ per faction.
Range (m) at which soldiers can hear a suppressed shot. Normal shots use the engine hearing distance. Can differ per faction.
After a close near miss (weight 0.8 or more), the soldier stays suppressed for this many seconds plus a random 3-6 s.

Suppression value (0.1-0.9) at or above which a soldier counts as suppressed, which shortens and lowers its moves. Suppressed soldiers also skip opportunity pushes. When tune_agg_profile is on, a higher aggression slider raises it slightly.
How strongly suppression affects the AI. 0 = immune.
Rate per second at which suppression and near-miss threat fade, further scaled by morale state. Higher means soldiers recover from suppression faster.
Multiplier on suppression gained from incoming fire while the soldier's morale is Panic or Break.
Multiplier on suppression gained from incoming fire while the soldier's morale is Shaken.
Multiplier on suppression gained from incoming fire while the soldier is in a spirited (high) morale state.
Multiplier on suppression gained from incoming fire while the soldier's morale is Tense.
Multiplier on suppression gained from incoming fire while the soldier is inside a building.
Multiplier on suppression gained from incoming fire while the soldier is in valid cover outside a building.
Multiplier on how fast suppression wears off while the soldier's morale is Panic or Break.
Multiplier on how fast suppression wears off while the soldier's morale is Shaken.
Multiplier on how fast suppression wears off while the soldier is in a spirited (high) morale state.
Audibility (1 at the shooter, 0 at max hearing range) at or above which a shot is always heard. Below it the chance is audibility divided by this value.
Most seconds to wait for assault slots to fill before the synchronized attack goes.
Groups gather at staging until full or timeout, then attack together.
The commander moves its attacking groups onto a still enemy-held objective only when the enemy count from tactic_consolidate_ring_m is at most this number. Checked every 10 s.
When the commander wants to consolidate on an objective the enemy still holds, it counts enemies within the objective radius plus this many metres.
Group posture. Automatic = decided from numbers, threat and morale.
Chance to actively seek cover when spotted in the open.

What each ordered group takes from the commander stock. No = only the force pool counts. Men = soldiers from the men counter. Points = cost from the points counter. Stock or pool empty = the spawner stops for good. Stock is taken when a group is ordered and given back if the order is cancelled.
Commander that receives the spawned groups: the weakest (lowest manpower per objective) or nearest commander of the chosen faction, or one specific commander.
Seconds before the same threat cluster can be shelled again. Default 90.

Marksmen and squad leaders point out what they see to the right specialist in their own squad: armor to the AT gunner, an enemy MG or a soldier in a building to the grenadier and MG, a group of infantry to the MG.
Soldiers pick targets by personality: who is shooting at them, AT/MG gunners, leaders/radio operators or the nearest enemy. At most one switch per 3 s.
Player groups of this faction get tasks (map and task list) for objectives this commander attacks or defends.

Quick choice of the jobs the AI commander may give this squad. Changing Allowed Tasks by hand shows Custom. Recon Only allows scouting and observation posts only. Reserve Only keeps the squad back for counterattacks, reinforcements and support for squads in trouble. Needs Commander Can Task.
Seconds between threat evaluations. Lower reacts faster. Default 45.
Distance (m) to group threats into one response cluster.
Radius (m) searched for contacts to find an objective's threat direction.
Seconds without new reports before a threat is forgotten. Default 60.

t: Threat Flank: From Friendly Contact Line
d: Counter-flank point is set about 90 degrees off the line between the friendly group in contact and the enemy, on the side nearer the flanking group (higher ground breaks ties). Off: the point is turned 55-80 degrees from the flanking group's own approach, which can put it on the same side as the friendly group.

t: Threat Flank: Route Around Enemy Front
d: When the straight run to the flank point would pass closer than 80% of the flank distance to the enemy, the group first goes to a detour point at the full flank distance, so it does not run across the enemy front.

Every threat think cycle (45 s) the final assault point of a counter-flanking group moves to the latest believed enemy position when the enemy has moved 30 m or more (Threat Flank Retarget Distance in the server config).
Distance (m) at which two reports count as the same threat.
Seconds ahead the threat's movement is projected to find the asset in its path.
Radius (m) for detecting enemies around this objective.

t: Threat: Big Groups Are Never Low Priority
d: A threat built only from small, harmless reports (2 or fewer enemies each) is normally ignored by the commander. On: once the whole cluster has 3 or more enemies, or its score is 1.5 times the response gate, the commander responds to it.
Seconds the leader of a player group has to accept or decline a commander offer card. No answer counts as declined: the job goes to AI groups, no penalty.
Aggression 0-2 (1 = normal): Attack versus defend share, counterattack, QRF tempo; shifts the force band and the doctrine attack ratio.
How much the commander values intel: chance to recon when the doctrine leaves it open, and caution on foggy objectives.
How early supply, reinforcement and medevac conditions trigger: sets when a group counts as Reduced and the low-ammo limit.
Strategy 0-2 (1 = normal): Threat versus objective weight, terrain objectives, flank instead of direct.
How early Support and Firesupport doctrine jobs trigger: sets when a group counts as Reduced and the low-ammo limit for those jobs.
DCO AI Commander that can use this vehicle for transport.
Transport is only used if it beats walking by at least this share.
Minimum travel distance (m) before a group looks for transport.
Logistics jobs this transport team may take. Transport = deploy, reinforce and redeploy. Resupply also needs a resupply station on the vehicle.

Fire rule for transport groups of this commander. Hold fire = only at enemies within about 50 m until the group is in contact. Tight = at relevant targets inside the engage distance. Free = at any target in range.
With Tight, transport groups open fire at relevant targets inside this distance (m). The commander personality scales it a little.
Objective whose ownership change triggers a spawn.

1 = soldiers leave cover at once when it stops protecting them, and attackers advance as soon as they are covered by friendly fire or the enemy goes quiet (max wait 25 s) instead of random 30-180 s cover waits. 0 = old timers.
On/off, default 0. Turning it on changes how the global aggression slider scales commander aggression: the trait value is scaled by the square root of the slider and may go above the normal limit.

On/off (default 0). When on, commanders use the K2 aggression model: the aiAggression slider scales the commander's attack odds, its wait times (tempo), the minimum attack force ratio and the retreat loss threshold, limited by the tune_agg_k2_* values. Also turns on the commander aggression profile.
Cap (0.5-1) on the commander's base attack chance from its personality before the aiAggression slider is applied. Used only when tune_agg_k2 is on.
Multiplier. Lowest force ratio a commander may require before attacking when a high aiAggression slider lowers the ratio. Used only when tune_agg_k2 is on.
Seconds. A high aggression tempo never shortens the doctrine recon timeout before an attack below this (or below the doctrine timeout if that is lower). Used only when tune_agg_k2 is on.

Fraction added to the doctrine retreat loss threshold per factor of 10 on the aiAggression slider (value x log10(slider)), so higher aggression means more losses before retreating; capped at 0.6 or the doctrine value. Used only when tune_agg_k2 is on.
Seconds. A high aggression tempo never shortens the commander's staging wait before an attack below this (or below the normal wait if that is lower). Used only when tune_agg_k2 is on.
Multiplier. Highest commander tempo (square root of aiAggression); limits how much a high slider shortens commander waits. Used only when tune_agg_k2 is on.
Multiplier. Lowest commander tempo (square root of aiAggression); waits are divided by tempo, so values below 1 let a low slider slow the commander down. Used only when tune_agg_k2 is on.
Seconds a group must wait before another post-grenade rush (a squadmate sprinting forward after a frag lands). Divided by the aggression slider. Used only when tune_agg_postfrag is on.
Seconds a group waits between pursuit moves toward an enemy that is pulling back. Divided by the aggression slider. Used only when tune_agg_pursue is on.
Metres an enemy must move away from the squad within about 3 seconds (heading away, two samples in a row) before the squad pursues it. Used only when tune_agg_pursue is on.
On/off, default 0. Turning it on stops the commander from giving new orders to a group that is breaking contact.
On/off, default 0. Turning it on makes commander tempo follow its aggression: higher tempo shortens staging waits and recon time limits before an attack.
Highest commander tempo factor (1-4). Higher means faster staging and recon for high-aggression commanders. Needs tune_cmd_aggr_tempo.
Lowest commander tempo factor (0.25-1). Lower means slower staging and recon for low-aggression commanders. Needs tune_cmd_aggr_tempo.

Cover scoring: metres added to a Defend waypoint's radius. On a Defend waypoint, cover spots farther than radius plus this from the waypoint, or more than the radius forward toward the enemy, are skipped. Used only when tune_cov_on is on.
Cover scoring: the most cover spots a soldier compares in one search. Higher = better choice but more CPU. Used only when tune_cov_on is on.
Cover scoring: the number of cover spots a soldier checks before he may stop searching and take the best one found so far. Used only when tune_cov_on is on.

Cover scoring: 1 = when a soldier looks for cover he compares several cover spots and picks the best by protection from the enemy, hard cover, distance, spacing from squadmates and (on a Defend waypoint) staying inside the defended area. 0 = he takes the game's first cover spot (old behaviour).
Cover scoring: metres. A cover spot closer than this to a squadmate is skipped so soldiers do not bunch up. Used only when tune_cov_on is on.
Cover scoring weight (0-10) for staying close to the Defend waypoint centre. Higher = defenders prefer cover nearer the middle of their position. Used only when tune_cov_on is on.
Cover scoring weight (0-10) against walking distance (counted per 30 m). Higher = soldiers prefer nearby cover over better cover farther away. Used only when tune_cov_on is on.
Cover scoring bonus (0-10) for hard cover such as walls, rocks and buildings over soft cover such as bushes. Used only when tune_cov_on is on.
Cover scoring weight (0-10) for how well the spot blocks the line of fire from the nearest known enemy (low, half or full body). Higher = protection matters more. Used only when tune_cov_on is on.
Cover scoring weight (0-10) for the game's own ranking of the cover spots. Higher = soldiers stick closer to the game's first choice. Used only when tune_cov_on is on.

Indoor close combat: 1 = a soldier moving to a chosen spot inside a building moves the spot off a doorway (by tune_cqb_door_push_m) instead of stopping in it, and runs when his path crosses a doorway. 0 = no doorway check (old behaviour). Used only when tune_cqb_kind_beh is on.
Metres a soldier's indoor move spot is pushed past a doorway so he does not stop in the door. Used only when tune_cqb_door_avoid and tune_cqb_kind_beh are on.
Metres. Maximum cover-search distance for one move when the soldier is in close combat inside a building. Used only when tune_cqb_kind_beh is on.
Metres. Shortest cover-search distance for one move in close combat inside a building, so a soldier does not make tiny steps. Used only when tune_cqb_kind_beh is on.

On/off (default 0). When on, soldiers with an enemy inside close-combat range (tune_tm_cqb_range_m) move differently indoors and outdoors: inside a building they take short bounds (tune_cqb_in_bound_m), run instead of sprint and avoid going prone; outside they search cover within tune_cqb_out_cover_m and, when no squadmate fired in the last 3 s, sidestep left or right (tune_cqb_out_lateral_m) instead of moving straight at the enemy, otherwise sprint.
Metres. Maximum cover-search distance for one move when the soldier is in close combat outside a building. Used only when tune_cqb_kind_beh is on.

Metres. Maximum distance of the left/right sidestep a soldier makes instead of moving straight toward a close enemy outdoors when no squadmate fired in the last 3 s. Used only when tune_cqb_kind_beh is on.
Metres. Shortest cover-search distance for one move in close combat outside a building. Used only when tune_cqb_kind_beh is on.
Outdoor close combat: 1 = a soldier's sprint toward the enemy is cancelled if no cover is found at the end of it. 0 = he sprints even without cover. Used only when tune_cqb_kind_beh is on.
Seconds. Longest time of one sprint to cover in close combat outside a building. Used only when tune_cqb_kind_beh is on.
On/off, default 0. Turning it on stops groups from trying to clear a building type after its room plan has failed tune_cqb_prefab_negcache_fails times.
Number of failed CQB room plans for a building type before that type is skipped. Needs tune_cqb_prefab_negcache.
On/off, default 0. Turning it on makes the reverse-slope defence crest search check two extra directions 25 degrees left and right of the threat axis.
Distance in metres beyond the objective radius within which defending groups may still attack or investigate an enemy cluster.
On/off (1 = on). Defending and garrison groups do not leave to attack or investigate enemy clusters farther than tune_def_engage_leash from their objective.

On/off (1 = on). Allows field fighting positions (scored outdoor spots with cover and line of sight) for garrison waypoints. Also required by tune_def_sector_garrison and tune_garrison_leftover_field.

On/off, default 0. Turning it on treats fighting-position spots with view under tune_def_fp_blind_m as having no cover. If no spot reaches tune_def_fp_min_los, it also searches further out toward the threat.
Line of sight in metres below which a fighting-position spot counts as blind and loses its cover score. Needs tune_def_fp_blind_fix.
Maximum distance in metres checked for line of sight when rating fighting positions. Score counts up to 150 m.
Line of sight in metres a fighting position should have. Spots below it get reduced cover score and a penalty.
Minimum distance in metres between chosen field fighting positions.
Score points added to a held objective that is contested when ordering which objective gets defenders first. Used only when tune_def_obj_priority is on.

On/off (default 0). When on, a defending commander assigns defenders to its held objectives in score order (objective value + nearby enemies x tune_def_obj_threat_w + tune_def_obj_contested_w if contested) instead of list order.
Score points added per enemy near a held objective when ordering which objective gets defenders first. Used only when tune_def_obj_priority is on.
Seconds threats from opposite sides must persist before the defence commander scores perimeter (all-round) defence higher.
Direction limit (-1 to 1, cosine of the angle) for a second threat axis to count as the opposite side of the main one. -0.17 is about 100 degrees apart; lower needs more opposite directions.
Completion radius in metres of the garrison waypoints the defence commander places for its groups.
On/off (1 = on). Commanders defending objective sectors place outward-facing garrison waypoints instead of plain defend waypoints. Needs tune_def_fieldpos.
Distance in metres beyond the objective radius at which the enemy crosses the trigger line. Defenders hold fire until then, unless suppressed or in close contact.
On/off, default 0. Turning it on makes combat fatigue also build (at half rate) while a soldier has a target within tune_fatigue_contact_m, and fade more slowly when out of contact.
Distance in metres to the current target within which contact builds fatigue. Needs tune_fatigue_contact_acc.

On/off (default 0). When on, the friendly-fire lane check for soldiers on foot uses the shooter's muzzle height by stance (standing, crouched, prone), so a friendly lying or crouching well below the line of fire no longer blocks the shot.
Seconds half of a group must be within the garrison waypoint radius + 10 m before the garrison starts. Needs tune_garrison_arrive_start.

On/off, default 0. Turning it on starts a garrison once half the group has been near the garrison waypoint for tune_garrison_arrive_s, and gives the garrison activity higher priority than vanilla defend.
On/off, default 0. Turning it on sends soldiers who got no building slot in a garrison to field fighting positions around the waypoint, if the waypoint allows field positions.
Priority added to the garrison activity above vanilla defend priority. Needs tune_garrison_arrive_start.
Maximum distance in metres to the target at which an attacking soldier may still throw a frag grenade under high threat. Used only when tune_gren_atk_close is on.
Multiplier on the vanilla threat limit for frag grenade throws. Attacking soldiers within tune_gren_atk_close_m may throw up to this multiple of the limit. Used only when tune_gren_atk_close is on.

Commander intel: 1 = the estimated number of enemies at an objective drops slowly when fewer are seen, does not rise without own eyes on the objective, and fades over time (half every 10 min) when nobody sees it. 0 = the estimate is replaced by each new count (old behaviour).

Strength of individual soldier learning (0-0.5). Learned results can change a position's score by up to this fraction up or down, and a soldier skips a cover spot whose learned score is below 1 - 0.6 x this value. Used only when tune_learn_ind_on is on.
Chance 0-1 that a soldier still uses a cover spot that individual learning marked as bad, so the spot keeps being re-tested. Used only when tune_learn_ind_on is on.

Individual learning freeze: 1 = soldiers use a separate fixed learning file (IndLearn/_frozen) and nothing new is saved, so behaviour stays the same between sessions. 0 = learning keeps updating and saving (old behaviour). Used only when tune_learn_ind_on is on.

Individual learning cover choice: 1 = a soldier compares up to 3 nearby cover spots and takes the one with the best learned score, 0 = he takes the game's first spot and only skips it if learning marked it as bad (old behaviour). Used only when tune_learn_ind_on is on.
Seconds after which an attacking soldier that is not pinned moves on from its stop even without covering fire. Used only when tune_mb_on is on.

Metres. A soldier waits (no advance, why=blast_wait) while a grenade thrown by his own squad in the last tune_mb_blast_s seconds landed within this distance of him; field positions within 15 m of such a blast are skipped. 0 = off. Used only when tune_mb_on is on.
Seconds a squad grenade blast point is remembered for tune_mb_blast_m (blast wait and field-position skip). Used only when tune_mb_on is on.
Seconds an attacking soldier stays at a new stop before the move brain lets it move again. Used only when tune_mb_on is on.
Number of near misses in the last 3 s that make a stopped soldier (stopped 1.5 s or more) leave the spot as compromised. Used only when tune_mb_on is on.
Radius in metres of the ring of 8 test points around a planned move spot used to find a covered field position. Used only when tune_mb_field is on.

Metres. 0 = off. When above 0, the Move Brain field-position search also tries a second ring of 8 points at this radius if fewer than 2 protected spots were found on the first ring. Used only when tune_mb_on and tune_mb_field are on.
Minimum distance in metres between a chosen field position and squadmates. Used only when tune_mb_field is on.
Minimum protection gain (score difference) the next spot must offer over the current one before a soldier makes a covered move. Used only when tune_mb_v2 and tune_mb_on are on.
Seconds a suppressed attacking soldier waits at its stop before moving on while covered by squad fire (or its fireteam's turn). Used only when tune_mb_on is on.
Seconds of running that set the maximum distance of one advance rush when picking a new spot (seconds x running speed). Used only when tune_mb_v2 is on.
Seconds of running for one advance rush when the soldier is suppressed (stress level 1 or higher); replaces tune_mb_rush_s in that case. Used only when tune_mb_v2 is on.

On/off (default 0). When on, soldiers pick advance spots by protection score within one rush distance (tune_mb_rush_s), crawl prone for 3 s when pinned and hit or exposed, and, with tune_mb_on, only make a covered move when the new spot gains at least tune_mb_gain_min protection.
Seconds after which a forced focus objective is cleared if the commander has not committed any groups to it.
For a forced focus objective, if doctrine keeps the commander in reconnaissance longer than this many seconds, it switches to movement to contact.
On/off (1 = on). When on, an operation against the commander's focus objective keeps its secondary (shaping) objectives. When off they are dropped and only the focus objective is planned.
On/off (1 = on). When on, objective phase rules apply: an objective becomes active for a faction only after its prerequisite objectives meet their condition and the activation delay has passed.

Seconds an attack-only commander waits for another commander's groups to arrive at the objective before handing it over to any non-offensive commander of the same faction allowed there. Used only when tune_obj_role_on is on.

On/off (1 = on). When on, commanders follow per-objective attack-only and defend-only roles: a defend-only commander does not attack that objective, and an attack-only commander hands the objective over to another commander for defence after capture.

Commander operations: 1 = a supporting objective that is neutral and has no enemy seen within 150 m of it is simply occupied instead of being covered by support-by-fire groups. 0 = support by fire as usual (old behaviour).
On/off (1 = on). AI says an 'under fire' voice line (at most once per 30 s per soldier) and a 'moving' callout when its fireteam or pursuit group starts a bound (at most once per 20 s per group).
On/off (1 = on). Soldiers who make an opportunity move (push, side-step, reload rush) call out 'moving' on the radio, and nearby squadmates who fired in the last 3 s answer 'covering'.

Longest time in seconds a soldier holds fire on a partly hidden enemy, waiting for a better shot, before firing anyway. Scaled x1.33 beyond 150 m and x0.67 closer. Used only when tune_opp_patient is on.
Seconds between suppressed-target pushes by the same soldier. Divided by the aggression slider. Used only when tune_opp_suppressed_push is on.
Closest distance in metres a push may bring a soldier to the target; no push starts when already within this distance plus 10 m. Used only when tune_opp_suppressed_push is on.

Seconds the target must have been quiet (not firing, not endangering the soldier) before a soldier may push forward on it. Divided by the aggression slider. Used only when tune_opp_suppressed_push is on.
Maximum distance in metres of one push move toward a suppressed target (minimum 10 m). Used only when tune_opp_suppressed_push is on.
Seconds between side-step moves a soldier makes against a distracted enemy (one looking away). Divided by the aggression slider. Used only when tune_opp_distracted is on.
Seconds. Shortest time one bound must last before the fireteams swap while a squad investigates a contact. Used only when tune_osc_fix_bound is on.
Seconds a soldier stays committed to a move before another order of the same importance can replace it. Used only when tune_osc_fix_commit is on.
Degrees. Half-width of the sector, centred on the move direction, in which a relocating soldier searches for cover near his destination. Used only when tune_osc_fix_cover is on.
Seconds a soldier reuses his last dodge direction when he reacts to fire again. Used only when tune_osc_fix_dir is on.
Seconds after a dodge during which a soldier may not dodge in the exact opposite direction. Used only when tune_osc_fix_dir is on.

Back-and-forth fix for squads investigating a contact: 1 = a fireteam that reaches its bound point too fast waits until the bound has lasted tune_osc_bound_min_s before the other team moves. 0 = teams swap at once (old behaviour).

Back-and-forth fix: 1 = a move order from a different reason of the same importance cannot replace a move started less than tune_osc_commit_s ago, and a repeat order to a nearby spot counts as the same move. 0 = any equal order replaces the current move at once (old behaviour).

Back-and-forth fix: 1 = on a long relocation move the soldier only searches for cover once he is near the destination, and then only in a sector toward it, so he does not turn back to cover behind him. 0 = cover search at the start, in any direction (old behaviour).

Back-and-forth fix: 1 = when a soldier reacts to gunfire or a hit, he keeps his last dodge direction for a while (tune_osc_dir_keep_s) and does not pick the exact opposite direction soon after (tune_osc_dir_noreverse_s). 0 = a new direction every time (old behaviour).

Back-and-forth fix: 1 = a relocation move without cover gets enough time to reach its destination (up to 30 s) and is resumed up to 3 times if the soldier stops more than 4 m short. 0 = the move can end early on its time limit (old behaviour).

Metres a soldier must move before the back-and-forth detector counts it as one leg of movement; a leg in the opposite direction counts as a reversal. Lower = more sensitive. Used only when tune_osc_on is on.
Back-and-forth movement detector, logging only: 1 = the server logs soldiers that reverse direction 3 times within 30 s without getting more than 8 m away. 0 = off. It does not change behaviour.
Seconds, default 2. A soldier must stay without a usable weapon or ammo for this long before he goes to pick up a weapon, so a short weapon switch or reload does not send him running to a corpse.
Seconds, default 120. A weapon the engine refused to equip, or that could not be reached, is skipped by everyone for this long.
On/off, default 0. Turning it on switches groups in a tactic to their execute-stage posture as soon as the commander releases the assault, even if they are still more than 150 m from the objective.

Rearm end rule: 1 = a soldier stops rearming once he has as many spare magazines as his starting loadout, or as soon as his inventory is full, and keeps what he took. 0 = he only stops at 3 spare magazines and otherwise keeps trying until the timeout (old behaviour).

Metres, default 2.5. The walk to an ammo box, corpse or dropped weapon counts as arrived within this distance, so the soldier starts taking ammo instead of standing next to an unreachable box centre until the 90 s timeout.

On/off, default 1. On: a soldier with exactly 1 spare magazine only goes to rearm if that is below the number of spare magazines he started with for this weapon (0 spare always triggers). Stops MG/AT gunners whose loadout has only 1 spare from running to ammo boxes at mission start. 0 = old rule (rearm at 1 spare for every weapon).
Reinforcements: 1 = when a recon group is requested but the spawner has no recon group, it sends its smallest group of up to 6 soldiers instead. 0 = the request stays unfilled (old behaviour).
Reinforcements: seconds after a defence reinforcement request for an objective ends before a new routine or priority request for the same objective can be made. Urgent requests ignore this.

Reinforcements: fraction (0-1) of the highest spawner stock seen that is kept in reserve. Routine and priority defence requests are refused while the stock is below it; urgent requests ignore this. 0 = no reserve.
Distance in metres under which the fast close-range reaction applies: a short attack wait before firing and reduced aim reset from suppression and morale drops. Used only when tune_rt_fast is on.
Multiplier (0-1) on how much incoming suppression and morale drops set back a soldier's aim on a target inside tune_rt_close_m. Lower keeps more aim.
Base wait in seconds before a soldier with low threat (surprised) fires at an enemy inside tune_rt_close_m. A small distance-based delay is added.
Base wait in seconds before a soldier who already feels threatened fires at an enemy inside tune_rt_close_m. A small distance-based delay is added.
Seconds after last attacking an enemy during which attacking the same enemy again starts with no wait.
Aim settle time in seconds for targets under 25 m, blending to 0.9 s at 50 m. Lower means faster accurate aim up close. Used only when tune_rt_fast is on.
Seconds, default 6. The MG assistant keeps his current move to the gunner for this long before he can be given a new spot, so he actually moves instead of being re-ordered every tick.
On/off, default 1. On: a machine gunner does not look for a new pre-contact firing position while he is rearming or picking up a weapon.
On/off (1 = on). When on, the commander checks that a support-by-fire position has line of sight to the objective and, if not, searches positions 120-280 m outside the objective radius that do.

Seconds a pursuing group keeps going with no known enemy near it before it gives up and returns to the captured objective. Used only when tune_tac_pursuit_track is on; shortened by commander aggression tempo.
Fraction (0.3-1) of the best tactic score that other tactics must reach to stay in the random pick pool. Higher means the top tactic is picked more often. Needs tune_tac_mett_on.
Intel confidence (0-1) below which the METT-TC table treats intel as partial; at or above it, intel counts as good.
Intel confidence (0-1) below which the METT-TC table treats intel on the objective as poor.
On/off, default 0. Turning it on makes commanders pick attack tactics from a METT-TC table that scores each tactic by intel, enemy, terrain, time and force ratio.
Score multiplier (0.1-1) for a tactic used within tune_tac_mett_recent_s. Lower means more variety.
Seconds during which a tactic the commander recently used gets a score penalty in the METT-TC pick.
Seconds a pursuing group may take to reach its pursuit point before it is called back to the captured objective. Used only when tune_tac_pursuit_track is off; shortened by commander aggression tempo.
Distance in metres beyond the objective radius that a tracking pursuit group may go before it returns. Needs tune_tac_pursuit_track.
Maximum seconds a tracked pursuit lasts before the group returns to the objective. Needs tune_tac_pursuit_track.

Multiplier. After an objective is captured, the commander starts a pursuit of retreating enemies only if its strength at the objective is at least this many times the estimated enemy count. Lowered by commander aggression tempo (not below 1.2).
Seconds between updates of a pursuit group's goal to the nearest known enemy. Needs tune_tac_pursuit_track.
On/off, default 0. Turning it on makes pursuit groups follow the nearest known enemy near the objective, within time and distance limits, instead of moving to one fixed point.
On/off, default 0. When a tactic group stops making progress, turning it on keeps the group's current route and forces aggressive posture for 90 s, instead of issuing a new assault order.

Same as tune_tac_stall_s, but for groups that are in contact: seconds without 15 m of progress toward the objective before the commander pushes the group forward. Shortened by commander aggression tempo (not below 30 s).

Seconds an attacking or flanking group (after the assault is released) may go without getting 15 m closer to the objective before the commander pushes it forward again. Used while the group is not in contact; shortened by commander aggression tempo (not below 30 s).
Minimum intel confidence (0-1) about the objective before a Siege or Attack-by-fire tactic may escalate. Used only when tune_tac_standoff_fix is on.

On/off (1 = on). When on, Siege and Attack-by-fire tactics do not escalate to an assault until tune_tac_standoff_min_s has passed and intel confidence reaches tune_tac_standoff_conf, even when the strength ratio is high enough.
Commander standoff: the longest time in seconds a commander keeps holding back because its confidence is too low before it must commit to the attack.
Minimum seconds a Siege or Attack-by-fire tactic runs before it may escalate. Used only when tune_tac_standoff_fix is on.
Maximum seconds one fireteam's bound may last before the turn passes to the other team. Used only when tune_tb_on is on.
Seconds a fireteam waits for its turn (other teams set and covering) before it is allowed to bound anyway. Used only when tune_tb_on is on.
Seconds after a fireteam member's last shot during which that team counts as giving covering fire, so the other team may bound. Used only when tune_tb_on is on.
Distance in metres from the maneuver team to the enemy at which squad fire-and-maneuver switches to the final assault with both teams moving. Used only when tune_tb_fm is on.
Squad fire and movement gate: if the assault element is already closer than this many metres to the enemy, it goes in at once without waiting for covering fire.
Squad fire and movement gate: the longest time in seconds the assault element waits for covering fire before it goes in anyway.
Seconds without a fresh enemy sighting after which squad fire-and-maneuver is cancelled. Used only when tune_tb_fm is on.
Maximum distance in metres from the base-of-fire team to the enemy for a squad fire-and-maneuver to start. Used only when tune_tb_fm is on.
Minimum distance in metres from the base-of-fire team to the enemy for a squad fire-and-maneuver (one team fires, one flanks) to start. Used only when tune_tb_fm is on.
Seconds a fireteam may hold its bounding turn without moving before the turn is ended. Used only when tune_tb_on is on.

Team bounding: a fireteam with a machine gunner stays in place as overwatch while another fireteam is within this many metres of it; when the other teams are farther away, the MG team bounds forward too. Used only when tune_tb_mg_ow is on.
On/off (1 = on). While the other fireteam is bounding, the overwatch team keeps suppressing an enemy it lost sight of for up to 30 s. Needs tune_tb_on.
Fraction 0-0.75 of a fireteam that may still be moving while the team counts as set (stopped) for team bounding. 0 = every member must have stopped. Used only when tune_tb_on is on.
Seconds without movement after which a fireteam counts as set (stopped) during fireteam bounding. Used only when tune_tb_on is on.
Target score penalty for each squadmate (counted up to 2) already shooting at the same enemy, so the squad spreads its fire. Used only when tune_tgt_claim is on.
Seconds a soldier's claim on a target stays valid after it last picked that target. Used only when tune_tgt_claim is on.

Metres. A counter-flank group's sweep waypoint is moved to the nearest known threat only if that threat is at least this far from the current flank target. Used only when tune_thr_flank_retarget is on.
Radius in metres around the current waypoint that an armed vehicle paired with infantry (armor pair) may move within when it looks for a fire position.
Ammo fraction (0-1) below which an armed vehicle skips reconnaissance fire on the enemy's last known position.

On/off (1 = on). When on, commanders may use armed vehicles (soft-skin, APC, tank) as support-by-fire groups, placed in a distance band by vehicle type with line of sight to the objective. Soft-skin vehicles are not used against likely anti-tank or MG threats, and only tanks are used against enemy armour.
Farthest distance in metres beyond the objective radius for an APC support-by-fire position. Used only when tune_veh_sbf is on.
Closest distance in metres beyond the objective radius for an APC support-by-fire position. Used only when tune_veh_sbf is on.

When anti-tank fire is likely (urban or forest objective, or enemy armour), APC and tank support-by-fire positions stay at least this many metres beyond the objective radius. Used only when tune_veh_sbf is on.
Maximum distance in metres from the objective at which a vehicle is picked for support by fire. Used only when tune_veh_sbf is on.
Farthest distance in metres beyond the objective radius for a soft-skin armed vehicle's support-by-fire position. Used only when tune_veh_sbf is on.
Closest distance in metres beyond the objective radius for a soft-skin armed vehicle's support-by-fire position. Used only when tune_veh_sbf is on.
Farthest distance in metres beyond the objective radius for a tank support-by-fire position. Used only when tune_veh_sbf is on.
Closest distance in metres beyond the objective radius for a tank support-by-fire position. Used only when tune_veh_sbf is on.

On/off, default 0. Needs tune_wp_attack_arrive on. Extends the arrive-complete rule (half the group inside the waypoint radius + 10 m for tune_wp_attack_arrive_s) from attack/flank to every task except defend, garrison, transport and fire mission (plain SCR_AIWaypoint only).
On/off, default 0. Turning it on completes an attack or flank group's waypoint once half the group has been within its completion radius + 10 m for tune_wp_attack_arrive_s.
Seconds half of an attack or flank group must stay inside the waypoint area before the waypoint is completed. Needs tune_wp_attack_arrive.
What the commander must do here: take it, destroy what is in it, or watch it. Defend: keep it against attacks. Hold until: keep it until the deadline.
Hold until and Destroy: seconds from mission start; the objective fails when this passes unfinished. 0 = no deadline.

Defend: the defending side (Auto = owner at mission start). Hold until: the side that must hold it (Auto = any side). Destroy: the side that must destroy the targets (Auto = any side that did not own it at start).
Defend: seconds from mission start the defenders must keep this objective. Hold until: seconds a side must own it without a break. Not used by Capture, Destroy or Recon.
Seconds the radius must be clear of enemies before it counts as uncontested.
Position error multiplier for contacts only detected, not identified. Can differ per faction.
When preparing a defence, garrison mode Hold is raised to Defend.
Below this share the request is urgent: arrival time halved and the spawner cooldown ignored. Below 0.25 the commander stops asking (the remnant is not refilled). FIA uses this value + 0.1.

Uses each commander's Retreat Threshold (minimum men per squad): a squad with that many men or fewer is pulled back to rebuild even before it falls under 40 % of its peak strength. Off: only the 40 % rule pulls squads back.
Specialist recovery may pick up enemy weapons.
Dismounts when danger is closer than this distance (m).

When this squad may leave its vehicles. Use global = follow the global Vehicle Exit setting (the boxes below then show the global choice). Untick it and pick your own boxes to give this squad its own rule, for example keep a tank crew inside while a truck squad dismounts. A destroyed or burning vehicle can always be left.

When AI may leave a vehicle. Ordered: Get Out waypoint, GM order or commander task. Vehicle damaged: below 50 % health. Danger: passengers = infantry in cargo seats dismount to fight. Danger: unarmed drivers = drivers of trucks and cars without a weapon. Danger: combat crew = driver, gunner and commander of armed vehicles (tanks, APCs, cars with a mounted gun). A destroyed or burning vehicle, or one below 25 %, can always be left. Static weapons and players are not affected. Default keeps combat crews in their vehicle. Squads can set their own rule.
Max distance (m) the squad fires at vehicles. Max 2500.
Idle armored groups and groups with their own vehicle patrol mounted: wider, slower, along roads.
Vehicle patrol radius multiplier compared to foot patrol. Default 2.5.
How far (m) the commander looks for a free transport vehicle near a group. Default 200.

Top speed for this squad's vehicle while AI drives it. 0 = use the faction AI Vehicle Speed Limit, or the engine default when that is 0 too. Overrides the commander's patrol speed. Applies immediately and follows the squad into a new vehicle.

Crewed: the vehicle comes with its own crew (driver, plus a gunner if it has a turret) and the group rides as passengers; the crew counts as men and points. Group mounts: the group drives the vehicle itself (old behaviour).
Extra position error for contacts passed by voice (rougher than radio).
Distance (m) a squad can shout a contact to another squad. No radio needed.
How long Wait lasts at Moderate decision before the objective is skipped (Fast halves it, Slow adds half). The required ratio rises 10 % per minute while the enemy digs in.
Multiplies the Weaker defence thresholds 0.33 (delay) and 0.17 (withdraw). Below 1 the defenders hold longer before they delay or withdraw.
Score weight for how protected the spot is. Can differ per faction.
Score weight for how good the firing direction is. Can differ per faction.
Score weight for closeness to the requested point. Can differ per faction.
Score weight for distance from other soldiers. Can differ per faction.
Soldiers in contact near a building take a window or roof slot facing the enemy.
Below this health (0-1) a vehicle leaves the fight. It also leaves after 2 rockets in 60 s, or when only one crew member is left.
Below this local strength ratio the response is delayed or withdraws.
